exchanges.question: Not an analyst exchange: this numbered block is the scripted management discussion that functions as the prepared remarks. Pooley presents Q3 results, segment results, industry outlook and FY2026 guidance, then asks Seibert, Norwood and Kovar for color on the quarter and tariffs, Construction & Forestry, Small Ag & Turf, Production & Precision Ag by region, model year 2027 early order programs, dealer inventories and precision technology adoption, before Norwood closes.
exchanges.answer: Pooley reported equipment operations operating margin of 14.4%, net sales and revenues up 5% to $12.608 billion, equipment net sales up 6% to $10.999 billion and net income of $1.379 billion or $5.10 per diluted share; FY2026 net income guidance was raised to $4.75 billion-$5 billion, equipment operations cash flow to $5 billion-$5.5 billion and Financial Services net income to $870 million, with PPA sales now down approximately 10% (margin 11%-12%), SAT up approximately 15% (margin raised to 14.5%-15.5%) and C&F up approximately 20% (margin 10.5%-11.5%). Seibert said factories exceeded production expectations, results beat company and consensus expectations, $110 million of incremental IEPA refunds were recognized in Q3 (total $382 million for FY2026, no further refunds assumed) and direct tariff expense is now approximately $1.1 billion for the year excluding refunds after Section 122, 232 and 301 changes; C&F order books are largely full with customer backlogs extending well into FY2027, production modestly below retail, factory-installed SmartGrade adoption up more than 50% year-to-date and job site safety sales up nearly 40%. Norwood said year-to-date performance and a strong fourth quarter order book across all segments allowed narrowed guidance and improved net income and cash flow forecasts, called C&F one of the most significant Leap Ambitions opportunities (including Tenna), and reiterated that 2026 represents the bottom of the ag equipment cycle with a measured, regionally varied recovery. Kovar said PPA demand is softer in South America and Europe but stable at very low levels in North America, order books are effectively full for the year, South America industry was revised to down 15%-20% with modest underproduction of retail there, and the move Agriculture Financing program plus lower rates should help 2027; the model year 2027 sprayer EOP opened mid-May and runs through the end of this month, planters opened at the beginning of June and close at the end of September, the combine program just opened, and collective planter and sprayer orders are up mid-single digits versus the completion of last year's program, with an update next quarter. She added that model-year 2023 and 2024 used high horsepower tractors are down nearly 40% from a year ago and the new-used value spread has largely normalized; See & Spray is on significantly more acres with more than 50% herbicide savings and factory adoption set to nearly double to about 1/3 of North American sprayers on order, more than 40% of North American model year 2027 planters include ExactRate, ExactShot and FurrowVision, Operations Center has more than 520 million engaged acres across nearly 1.2 million connected machines, more than 190 million highly engaged acres (double-digit growth) and more than 450,000 unique active monthly digital users, with AI-enabled capabilities coming soon, and seed, fertilizer and crop protection are roughly 70% of a farmer's operating cost.

exchanges.question: For the 2027 setup, how is Deere thinking about production versus retail by region? And given the early order program is up mid-single digits, what are pricing expectations for 2027 in light of concerns about inflationary farm equipment costs over the past several years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said PPA and C&F are each modestly underproducing retail this year, call it a couple percentage points per segment; shipping plans are set for the full year, changes in South America drive more caution there, and in C&F continued retail growth with an order position four to five months out leads to minor underproduction in 2026. Kovar said EOP pricing was rolled out several months ago and the focus remains on covering inflation with pricing, which has been done across the EOP products and the whole PPA portfolio heading into 2027.

exchanges.question: Is the reduction in expected tariff impact to $1.1 billion, about $100 million below the original estimate, a function of the ag equipment tariff relief in July or of expected refunds? Second, how is the excavator launch trending and when will broader adoption happen?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said the FY2026 direct tariff run rate was previously $1.2 billion and is now $1.1 billion, excluding refunds, driven mainly by Section 232 changes that cut the rate on imported goods from roughly 25% to 15%, notably on imports from Europe; the changes were effective 1st June so only five of 12 months benefit this year, implying a further tailwind in FY2027. Norwood said the first Deere-designed excavator models launched earlier this spring, three models are in the market with very positive customer feedback, shipments are just getting into customers' hands, and additional models in the portfolio will roll out over the next three to four years.

exchanges.question: Did something slip from 4Q into 3Q, and why do inventory-to-sales ratios suggest tractor inventory was built in 3Q ahead of the industry? Is that an offset to demand signals in South America, and what is the cadence exiting the year?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said not to read too much into Q3 changes: shipment plans are largely set for the year with orders on hand, some demand was pulled ahead to manage Q4 risk, and there is nothing concerning on inventory. Kovar said factories are hitting forecasts, sold-ahead positions and retail pace across the Americas are on trend with historical averages, and North America entered the year slowly on tractor shipments (she said 2027) and is making up time while retail pace has not missed. Norwood said PPA and C&F should see Q4 net sales similar to Q3, but Q4 will not have the refund benefit Q3 had and PPA and SAT typically carry a seasonal high of R&D and SA&G in Q4, so margins for those two segments will come in a little.

exchanges.question: How should the mix impact in 2027 be thought about, given higher technology take rates in the early order program and in C&F, versus the 2- to 3-point mix benefit discussed in stronger years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell: input and commodity volatility, shipment disruptions such as the Black Sea, and recent softness in the E.U. and Brazil need to play out, and construction growth could also affect mix. EOP signals including tech adoption and how the programs wrap up will drive some mix, along with whether the recovery is more than modest and what combines do later this year; he is encouraged by current signals.

exchanges.question: What regional variability in demand did the early order program show, and as it winds down could the current mid-single-digit growth end up in the high single-digit range?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said the programs are still open with a couple of weeks left on sprayers and longer on planters; the U.S. is trending slightly better than Canada, which is a very limited part of the planter portfolio. Orders are up mid-single digits and time will tell whether that turns more positive by close. The best signals are technology take rates: See & Spray doubling on factory-installed sprayer orders and 40% of planters taking the most advanced planting technologies.

exchanges.question: What has the cadence of early order program orders looked like since the books opened, and was the mid-single-digit increase driven by recent grain price improvement or technology decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said she would not read much into cadence, which has been as expected. Deere made tweaks to the early order program this year to give dealers more choice, orders have come through as expected, technology take rates were a pleasant surprise, and she hopes the mid-single-digit increase extends well into the year.

exchanges.question: Are 8 Series tractor orders tracking the better early order program trend in North America? And in Europe, are crop prices starting to reflect farmer stress from heat and input costs, and would Europe react to a crop price response the way the U.S. does?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said 8R orders are as expected, with orders four to five months out, the model year 2026 shipment schedule basically closed and first-quarter orders now being collected; corn futures at about $5.05 are a good signal for growers. In Brazil Deere takes a three-month order book, has fourth quarter orders on hand, has changed its industry guide, and it is too early to tell on 2027, though the move financing program at single-digit rates could drive momentum. Europe is mixed, with arable farmers more challenged while Small Ag & Turf producers benefit from relatively strong and stable dairy and livestock cash flows; overall order pace is as expected with no step-up in the last one or two days.

exchanges.question: How are the Construction & Forestry order programs shaping up, how much of the strength is dealer rental fleet loading, and what is the outlook for that theme?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said C&F order trends have been very positive with about four to five months of orders on hand, more than the two to three months Deere would typically want, supported by industry and retail growth. Drivers are large infrastructure projects, data center starts, participation in the independent rental channel and the dealer-owned rental fleet opportunity, and the 2026 underproduction gives a little additional opportunity entering 2027.

exchanges.question: With the Section 232 benefit only a half year in 2026 and no further refunds in Q4, is the roughly $800 million net tariff impact this year a headwind, tailwind or neutral going into 2027?
exchanges.answer: Norwood said net tariffs will be a headwind next year: about $1.1 billion of direct tariffs this year less $382 million of refunds gives net exposure of approximately $750-ish million, while the 2027 run rate is expected to be right around $1 billion, so tariff expense steps up next year.

exchanges.question: Why does C&F pricing guidance imply only about 50 basis points of positive price for Q4 versus +8% in Q3? Second, what size does Deere want its dealer rental fleet business to reach and how does it change the economics of the business?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said the C&F price guide started the year at 2.5%, went to 3%, was rounded down to 2.5% and is now back up at the full-year guide; Q3's 8% partly reflected easy comps because Q3 2025 had about 5% negative price from competitive incentives, Q4 orders are on hand with nothing outsized year over year, and pricing including road building is going well. Norwood said 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental and that share keeps growing; dealer-owned fleets have grown with the market and dealers show increased appetite to expand them, a meaningful opportunity that could help boost inventory fill next year, with no target size given.

exchanges.question: On EOP pricing covering inflation, are there merchandising incentives, and does the backlog imply margins up, down or neutral going into next year? Second, what are the implications of the FTC right-to-repair settlement for the aftermarket business and the $2 billion-$3 billion lifecycle parts opportunity over five years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said Deere is taking measured inflationary price in a challenging environment with nothing outsized, committed to covering inflation over time across several pricing points in the year (tractor order book, combine EOP), while the inflationary environment remains dynamic given oil prices and suppliers passing on tariffs; he gave no margin direction. Norwood said Deere has always supported customers' ability to repair their own equipment or use third parties, the agreement formalizes existing tools such as John Deere Operations Center PRO Service (diagnostic tools, digital manuals, self-service software updates or via independent service advisors), and it will support long-term lifecycle solutions aspirations.

exchanges.question: With the European CAP budget policy change set for 2028, could demand be pulled forward into 2027 or delayed until there is certainty, and can Deere give any directional 2027 forecast for Europe?
exchanges.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell; the order book runs four to five months out and Q1 orders are just starting to be collected. Arable producer sentiment will depend on input costs and commodity prices for next year's crop, dairy and livestock look fairly stable, and it is too early to say whether policy will pull demand forward or delay it.

exchanges.question: How are Brazilian and U.S. farmers positioning on input costs, particularly fertilizer, and how might that affect crop and equipment decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag
exchanges.answer: Kovar said input price uncertainty exists everywhere and fertilizer affects Brazilian and U.S. farmers differently, but markets are reacting and farmers are seeking alternatives in product type, application rates and sourcing. Deere is not seeing a huge reduction in intended application, farmers remain focused on yield, and larger farmers with multiple years of inputs contracted are considering changes; overall farmers remain resilient and nimble.

summary.overview: Apple reported a June quarter record revenue of $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, driven by strong iPhone and Mac demand. Management provided September quarter revenue growth guidance of 9%-11%, citing sequential FX headwinds and increased supply constraints on advanced nodes.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook announced this is his final earnings call, with John Ternus taking over as CEO for future calls.
September quarter revenue is expected to grow by 9%-11% year-over-year, with an FX headwind of 2.5 percentage points.
Supply constraints are impacting iPhone, Mac, and iPad due to unprecedented demand exceeding forecasts for advanced SoCs.
Apple reluctantly raised product prices due to exponential memory cost increases described as a 100-year flood.
financialHighlights: Total revenue reached $109.4 billion, representing an increase of 16% year-over-year.
Diluted earnings per share were $2.02, up 29% from $2.01 in the prior-year period.
Company gross margin expanded 80 basis points sequentially to reach 50.1%.
Operating cash flow for the quarter was reported at $34.4 billion.
guidance: Total company revenue year-over-year growth is projected at 9%-11% for the September quarter.
iPhone reported growth rate year-over-year is expected to be mid-teens for the September quarter.
Gross margin is guided to be between 47% and 48% for the September quarter.
Operating expenses are expected to range from $19.1 billion to $19.4 billion for the September quarter.
Other income and expense (OIE) is forecasted at around $350 million for the September quarter.

qa.question: Can you discuss how much of the September revenue decel is due to supply constraints versus FX, and flesh out the supply constraints?
qa.answer: Kevan Parekh stated that September total revenue is expected to grow by 9%-11%, impacted by a 2.5 percentage point FX headwind and increased supply constraints on iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Tim Cook added that constraints are driven by high demand and limited flexibility on advanced node SoCs.

qa.question: Could you talk about expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and if the new Siri AI will be a demand driver for iPhones this holiday while informing compute costs and iCloud+ recovery?
qa.answer: Tim Cook noted that the Apple Upgrade Program has positive early feedback in the U.S. and that developer and public beta feedback for Siri AI is overwhelmingly positive. He stated that compute cost impacts are in early stages, with potential upgrade possibilities on iCloud+.

qa.question: How much do supply constraints impact December, and can you broaden silicon providers in a reasonable timeframe to alleviate supply?
qa.answer: Tim Cook explained the constraints are driven by advanced node demand outpacing forecasts due to stronger-than-expected iPhone and Mac performance, while Kevan Parekh declined to provide color beyond September. Cook emphasized it is a product cycle demand issue, not a supplier problem, and noted over 100 million components are sourced from Arizona this year.

qa.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for supply and pre-agreed prices, and what is your thought process on product pricing for gross margins or dollars?

exchanges.question: Can you discuss how much of the September revenue decel is due to supply constraints versus FX, and flesh out the supply constraints?
exchanges.answer: We expect September total revenue to grow by 9%-11% year-over-year, impacted by a sequential 2.5 percentage point FX headwind and increased supply constraints. The projected supply constraints affect iPhone, Mac, and iPad, combining to bring us close to the June growth rate. Tim Cook added that the constraints are driven by very high demand and limited flexibility in the supply chain, primarily on advanced nodes for SoCs.

exchanges.question: Could you talk about expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and if the new Siri AI will be a demand driver for iPhones this holiday while informing compute costs and iCloud+ recovery?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade makes it easier for customers to get our latest products with a leasing plan, and early feedback is quite positive, though it is only available in the U.S. right now. On Siri AI, we are off the charts excited with overwhelmingly positive feedback from developer and public betas, believing it is a very big idea. Regarding compute costs, it is early going, but we believe people will want to use it a lot and we will have upgrade possibilities on iCloud+.

exchanges.question: How much do supply constraints impact December, and can you broaden silicon providers in a reasonable timeframe to alleviate supply?
exchanges.answer: The primary issue is advanced nodes for our SoCs, driven by a demand forecast issue due to iPhone and Mac doing remarkably better than thought. Kevan Parekh added we are not providing color beyond the September quarter. Tim Cook stressed that this is not a partner or supplier issue, but an incredible product cycle yielding demand beyond expectation, and noted we source over 100 million components from Arizona this year.

exchanges.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for supply and pre-agreed prices, and what is your thought process on product pricing for gross margins or dollars?
exchanges.answer: We reluctantly raised prices because we are in a 100-year flood on memory pricing with exponential increases. In terms of our philosophy, we look at units, revenue, and margin over the long term and come to a business judgment rather than using a mathematical formula. Kevan Parekh also addressed services growth, noting FX was the main driver of the change and mentioning mobile gaming headwinds and a lack of theatrical release compared to last year.

exchanges.question: How do you assess whether there is any pull-forward of demand from consumers, enterprise, or education, and do you see AI opening up additional addressable markets over time?
exchanges.answer: iPhone has been running at 22% growth year to date, and it is not obvious in the data that there is a pull-forward of demand. For price elasticity on iPad and Mac after price increases, it is too early to come to a definitive conclusion because it takes time for channels and consumers to respond. On AI, there are enormous opportunities for Apple moving forward, and running requests on-device is highly strategic.

exchanges.question: Do you expect Siri AI to change Apple's capital intensity, and how do you see the competitive landscape evolving with competitors building devices?
exchanges.answer: We use a hybrid model with third-party cloud and our own data centers, and while we are growing OpEx and spending more on AI across P&L locations, the balance and cost impact are uncertain at the moment. John Ternus added that there is so much opportunity for us with everything happening in this space and we are focused on our plans.

In China, we received approval to ship original features of Apple Intelligence last week and are working through the rollout. summary.overview: JPMorgan Chase reported fiscal Q2 2026 net income of $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per share, with a ROTCE of 23%. Revenue grew 15% year-on-year, driven by exceptional performance in equities and strong wholesale and consumer deposit trends. Management raised full-year NII and expense guidance while addressing recent executive co-president appointments and long-term operating leverage.
keyTakeaways: Jamie Dimon noted that the board appointed Doug and Troy as co-presidents to prepare them for greater responsibilities, which did not change the CEO timetable and preceded Marianne Lake's retirement.
Full-year NII ex-Markets was revised upward to $96.5 billion, primarily driven by stronger wholesale and consumer deposit balances along with slight rate support.
Jeremy Barnum stated that wholesale deposit growth outperformed expectations due to franchise strength, while consumer deposits expect low single-digit growth for the year.
Jamie Dimon emphasized that perpetual operating leverage is not guaranteed when maintaining high returns and margins, and that AI benefits will largely accrue to customers over time.
financialHighlights: Net income reached $16.9 billion with EPS of $6.14 and an ROTCE of 23%.
Total net revenue (ex-significant items) increased by 15% year-on-year, while total expenses were $27.3 billion, up 15% year-on-year.
Credit costs totaled $2.5 billion, comprising $2.4 billion in net charge-offs and a net reserve build of $149 million.

CCB generated $5.3 billion in net income on revenue of $20.3 billion, CIB generated $9.7 billion in net income on revenue of $24.9 billion, and AWM delivered $2 billion in net income on $6.9 billion in revenue.

exchanges.question: Can you discuss deposit growth progression towards the 15% retail market share and how higher-for-longer rates impact market share gains?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposit growth has outperformed expectations due to franchise strength and lending environments. Consumer deposit growth expects low single-digit growth for the year, balancing strong checking account growth and yield-seeking flows. The 15% retail market share remains a natural long-term consequence of executing the core strategy.

exchanges.question: What are the drivers of the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and the cadence for Q3 and Q4?

exchanges.question: What characteristics are the board looking for in the new CEO, and should Marianne's departure be read as an extension of your tenure?
exchanges.answer: The leadership qualities desired include strong management, analytical skills, detail orientation, culture carrying, curiosity, grit, work ethic, and adaptability. The succession timetable remains essentially the same, spanning a few years, entirely up to the board.

exchanges.question: Given heavy investments in AI and technology, is there an intermediate-term period where expense growth could slow and operating leverage becomes more likely?
exchanges.answer: Perpetual operating leverage is not guaranteed nor expected when maintaining great returns and margins. Expense growth could potentially slow in 2027 or 2028, and the ultimate beneficiary of AI will be customers rather than internal margins.

exchanges.question: Is current performance as good as it gets, and at what point does deposit behavior change given fluctuating rate expectations?
exchanges.answer: It is getting close to as good as it gets, though the duration remains unknown. Consumer deposit behavior includes negative convexity risks that are accounted for in stress testing and models even if betas have been better than expected.

exchanges.question: Is operating leverage negative the right way to view things, and what gives confidence that Troy can run consumer banking without prior experience in it?
exchanges.answer: Revenue growth drove positive dollar operating leverage. Troy's analytical power, EQ, brain power, and culture-carrying ability across markets and investment banking give full confidence in his ability to lead consumer banking.

exchanges.question: Are we vastly underestimating AI's potential benefits to efficiency, and what was most exceptional about equities this quarter?
exchanges.answer: AI will yield huge efficiencies and includes around 1,000 use cases with 50 primary ones across risk, fraud, and marketing, though benefits largely accrue to customers. The equities quarter reflected exceptional dynamics like major IPOs, index rebalancing, and Korean equity market activity.

exchanges.question: What are you seeing on Main Street consumer resiliency, and why buy back stock at 3x tangible book instead of holding excess capital for a rainy day?
exchanges.answer: Consumer spend is robust across income segments with tax refunds acting as a tailwind and delinquencies lower than expected. Capital deployment targets organic growth and infrastructure needs across global deficits, remilitarization, and technology, with buybacks treated as investment decisions.

exchanges.question: What is the status of the smart cash tool, and what are your European consumer banking aspirations?
exchanges.answer: The smart cash tool is still in a test phase targeting a narrow segment of accounts, with something launching this year. European digital banking operations in the UK and Germany are expanding with high hopes for a pan-European digital bank over time.

exchanges.question: What are you seeing in credit underwriting from competitors, and could we enter a period of regulatory stability that enhances bank valuations?
exchanges.answer: Competitive pressures exist in areas like data center underwriting with normal negotiation, but no massive deterioration is cited. Regulatory stability is desirable, and oscillations may decrease as regulators refocus on safety and soundness.

exchanges.question: Are you pulling forward any tech or marketing spend given the environment, and how nimble do you expect to be with CIB capital allocation?
exchanges.answer: Some tech and marketing spend adjustments occur dynamically, and token expense is forecast to accelerate in the second half though remaining trivial. CIB capital allocation responds to direct client demand rather than acting as a static hedge fund pot.

keyTakeaways: Mounjaro and Zepbound achieved $14.9 billion in combined global revenue, contributing $6.3 billion of growth compared to Q2 2025.

exchanges.question: How does Lilly envision expanding consumer treatment opportunities going forward, and how unique or similar is the U.S. versus international self-pay market?
exchanges.answer: Utilization of obesity care remains at mid-single digits, offering significant runway. In the U.S., about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay, and Lilly is leveraging consumer awareness campaigns and LillyDirect to expand access and affordability. Outside the U.S., the obesity market is primarily out-of-pocket, and Lilly is replicating U.S. practices and expanding local versions of LillyDirect while adhering to local regulations.

exchanges.question: What are the contributing factors to the slower-than-anticipated U.S. launch curve for Foundayo, and what are the learnings regarding ex-U.S. competitive dynamics and trajectory compared to rivals like Novo Nordisk?
exchanges.answer: Foundayo progress involves physician education, access, and DTC awareness, with the last week of July showing a clear inflection point, nearly doubling volume from a month prior and capturing one out of four new starts. Outside the U.S., early uptake in the UAE shows orals expand the market with many treatment-naive patients, and combined incretin share has held steady despite second entrants, with major OUS launches slated for 2027.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones ahead for ensuring retatrutide is accepted as a BLA, and is this pathway unique or applicable to subsequent incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly maintains retatrutide qualifies as a biologic application under amino acid count rules and protein analogy. Active litigation is ongoing, but Lilly hopes to reach a resolution with the FDA. Clinical data packages are complete, and additional CMC data is being gathered ahead of a targeted U.S. submission in Q1 2027.

exchanges.question: What are the early learnings, surprises, and ramp curves from the Medicare Obesity rollout, and what are the trends between orals and injectables?
exchanges.answer: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program has increased access for about 35% more Americans. Early trends show a significant inflection point, with about 80% of patients choosing injectables and roughly 60%-70% being new patients without prior access.

exchanges.question: Do you need a commercial strategy to protect against available products today for retatrutide, and does retatrutide's higher efficacy unlock new indications?
exchanges.answer: Patients will vote for authentic retatrutide once available. High-dose retatrutide unlocks additional indications like osteoarthritis knee pain, demonstrating a 75% pain reduction in trials, alongside ongoing evaluations in MASH/MASLD and chronic lower back pain.

exchanges.question: How is Lilly thinking about the post-Verzenio breast cancer strategy, and is an all-oral combination of SERD and oral PI3K on the table?
exchanges.answer: Lilly targets estrogen receptor, CDK4/6, and PI3 kinase alpha with products like INLURIYO and tersolisib. Plans include combining them over time in various settings, including with investigator choice of CDK4/6 like Verzenio for an all-oral combination.

exchanges.question: Does guidance imply a deceleration in revenues for the back half of the year, or is management being conservative given Medicare Bridge and Foundayo access?
exchanges.answer: The full-year revenue guide was upgraded by $2.5 billion. Factors affecting back-half comparisons include non-recurring pre-period rebate adjustments from prior quarters and the base period bolus of OUS MOUNJARO country launches from 2025. Absolute dollar growth remains robust, with future OUS growth driven by market penetration and seasonality factors like European summer holidays and U.S. Type 2 diabetes dynamics.

exchanges.question: Which specific regions are seeing the most OUS growth, and what are the dynamics in India with generic launches and supply constraints?
exchanges.answer: Strong performance is observed broadly, highlighted by China NRDL category leadership after 16 months, and strong growth in Korea, the U.K., Mexico, and Germany. In India and Brazil, TRx for MOUNJARO continues to grow despite generic semaglutide due to clinical differentiation, while generic suppliers experience supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the Foundayo sampling program, is it dampening IQVIA prescription data, and what is the expansion of the U.S. prescribing base?
exchanges.answer: Sampling covers the first 30 days for the first dose, typical for oral small molecules, backed by full supply. The prescribing base has expanded from 8,000 to 36,000 prescribers, with week-on-week adoption growth.

exchanges.question: How sustainable is net pricing and medical exception dynamics for obesity, and does CVS formulary return drive favorable rebate adjustments?
exchanges.answer: Zepbound prices are transparent through channels like LillyDirect and the Bridge program. Medical exceptions are a short-term driver, but open access is the goal, and CVS access starting in Q4 will reduce medical exception reliance, which is fully embedded in guidance and offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines high-priority M&A areas that Lilly can scale, or are they one-off asset plays driven by science?
exchanges.answer: Both areas share immense unmet need, driving internal and business development work. Acquisitions focus on impactful technology and medicines at disciplined prices to create long-term value, with future deals remaining opportunistic.

exchanges.question: What specific pipeline products outside obesity should the street pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Highlights include cardiovascular ASCVD gene editing for PCSK9, oral and injectable Lp(a)-lowering drugs, sleep-wake disorders with Centessa, oncology readouts including Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor, and immunology expansion for lebrikizumab and IBD combinations.

exchanges.question: What is the ex-U.S. potential for Foundayo obesity following UAE performance, and how will ex-U.S. government reimbursement for diabetes compare to tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: UAE start is encouraging, though inventory build plays a role, with major OUS rollouts starting in early 2027. Orals may be slightly better positioned for Type 2 diabetes reimbursement given head-to-head clinical data, though reimbursement OUS always requires time.

summary.overview: Apple reported fiscal Q3 2026 total revenue of $109.4 billion, an increase of 16% year-over-year, alongside record net income of $29.8 billion and diluted EPS of $2.02. Results were driven by 22% growth in iPhone to $54.3 billion and 29% growth in Mac to $10.4 billion, while the company absorbed mounting memory component inflation and supply shortages. Tim Cook marked his final earnings call before incoming CEO John Ternus takes the helm.
keyTakeaways: Total revenue reached a June-quarter record $109.4 billion, up 16% year-over-year, driven by products expanding 18% to $78.7 billion.
Gross margin reached 50.1%, aided by an approximate 2.0 percentage point benefit from tariff refunds.
Tim Cook confirmed his retirement from earnings calls, transitioning leadership to incoming CEO John Ternus.
Severe supply bottlenecks in advanced node SoC capacity are affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad deliveries into the September quarter.
Rising DRAM costs prompted selective hardware price increases, which Tim Cook characterized as driven by a '100-year flood' in memory inflation.
financialHighlights: iPhone revenue set a June-quarter record of $54.3 billion, growing 22% year-over-year.
Mac revenue rose 29% year-over-year to $10.4 billion, while iPad revenue declined 6% to $6.2 billion.
Services revenue increased 12% year-over-year to a June-quarter record $30.7 billion, supported by over 1.5 billion paid subscriptions.
Operating expenses totaled $19.1 billion, representing a 23% increase year-over-year.
Operating cash flow reached a June-quarter record of $34.4 billion, supporting $33 billion in total capital returns including $25.8 billion in share buybacks.

exchanges.answer: Sequentially into September, foreign exchange is an approximate 2.5 percentage point headwind to year-over-year total company growth, alongside a significant sequential increase in supply constraints affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Tim Cook added that constraints are driven by high demand and limited availability of advanced nodes for SoCs. exchanges.question: What are your expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and how are early public beta learnings on Siri AI informing compute cost planning and monetization via iCloud+?

exchanges.question: How significantly will supply constraints impact the December quarter, and could Apple broaden silicon suppliers, such as the fab in Arizona, to alleviate constraints?

Kevan Parekh stated Apple provides no guidance beyond September. exchanges.question: What is the thought process behind recent price increases and multi-year LTAs, and what factors are driving the deceleration in services growth into the September quarter?
exchanges.answer: Price increases were reluctantly implemented due to a '100-year flood' of exponential memory cost increases, balancing units, revenue, and margins over the long term. Kevan Parekh explained services growth was impacted sequentially by FX (a 2.5 percentage point sequential headwind, and 5 points from March to September), the tough compare against last year's F1 theatrical release, softness in mobile gaming, and business model adjustments for court rulings regarding U.S. link-outs.

exchanges.question: Are you seeing any pull-forward of demand given memory pricing dynamics, and does edge AI open up new addressable markets over time?
exchanges.answer: With iPhone tracking at 22% growth year-to-date, there is no obvious evidence of demand pull-forward in the data, though it is too early to determine consumer elasticity from recent Mac and iPad price increases. Cook sees enormous opportunities from edge AI and highlighted the strategic advantage of running requests on-device.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI alter Apple's capital intensity given its distributed architecture, and how does the incoming CEO view potential competitive threats from emerging AI devices?
exchanges.answer: Apple operates a hybrid infrastructure model combining first-party data centers and third-party cloud, with increased AI expenditures occurring across OpEx and COGS that may be offset by iCloud plan upgrades. Incoming CEO John Ternus responded that Apple sees massive opportunity in the space and remains focused on its own plans.

exchanges.answer: In the EU, Apple is working with the European Commission to reach a solution (Mac is not covered by the same regulations and will receive Siri AI), while in China, Apple received approval last week to ship baseline Apple Intelligence features with Siri AI still requiring future work. summary.overview: Chipotle reported second-quarter revenue of $3.3 billion, up 9.3%, with comparable restaurant sales increasing by 2.2% and digital sales reaching $1.3 billion. Restaurant-level margins contracted to 25.2%, down 220 basis points year-over-year, while adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.33. Management raised full-year comparable restaurant sales guidance to the low single-digit range based on year-to-date performance and Q4 expectations.
keyTakeaways: Traffic improved through Q2 and into early July, though the second half of July softened by about 200 basis points due to an industry issue regarding Cyclospora.
The High-Efficiency Equipment Packages save two to four hours of efficiency and contribute to throughput gains, with HEAP restaurants producing two to four extra entrees in Max 15.
Younger and lower-income cohorts improved the most relative to higher income, driven by menu innovation like Chipotle Honey Chicken and promotions like Matchday BOGO.
Company-operated openings are targeted at approximately 350 per year to ensure sustainable growth, complemented by partner-operated global expansion models.

qa.answer: Chipotle Honey Chicken performed better the second time around. Brand tracker data showed solid progress across all income groups and age cohorts on value perception, and affordability scores were better in Q2 than in the past couple of years.

qa.question: Can you provide color on the full year comp guide and the trajectory of recent weeks, including softening?

whatChanged.toneShift: The language shifted to reflect cautious optimism regarding raised full-year guidance despite acknowledged transient headwinds from Cyclospora issues in July.

risksMentioned: An industry issue regarding Cyclospora softened the second half of July comps by about 200 basis points.
Cost of sales inflation is running at a low single-digit range with cost of sales at 29.7%.

exchanges.question: Can you discuss bringing back LTOs from the pantry and whether the lift from Chicken al Pastor is as good or better than before, and are you seeing any changes in value perception?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle Honey Chicken performed better the second time around, as do many of our LTOs. Brand tracker data showed really solid progress across all income groups and age cohorts on value perception, and affordability scores were better in Q2 than in the past couple of years.

exchanges.question: How do you know comps are going to pick up into 2027 given the spending and effort for 1% to 2% comp growth lately, and where does your confidence come from?
exchanges.answer: Transaction growth in Q2 was the early days of our Recipe for Growth strategy. Investments in restaurant execution, High-Efficiency Equipment Packages, menu innovation, deeper rewards engagement, and stronger brand communications are showing green shoots and will scale as the year unfolds.

exchanges.question: Can you provide color on the full year comp guide and the trajectory of recent weeks, including softening?
exchanges.answer: Traffic improved through Q2 and into early July, but the second half of July softened by about 200 basis points due to the industry issue regarding Cyclospora. Q3 comps are anticipated around plus 1%, assuming a continuation of that headwind, but year-to-date performance and Q4 expectations gave confidence to raise guidance to low single-digits.

exchanges.question: Have you been able to size up incremental costs and expected sales uplifts for store refreshes, and have you considered leveraging partners in other international markets instead of owning and operating?
exchanges.answer: Store refresh investments are in early stages across selected locations, targeting between $100,000 to $300,000 per restaurant to test consumer perceptions and returns. For international expansion, we will own and operate Western Europe and build strategic partner-operated models or joint ventures for the rest of the world.

exchanges.question: What drove the 18% digital sales growth, and are changes in loyalty and ability to pay linked?
exchanges.answer: The initiatives are all linked; the Summer of Extras launch informed our rewards refresh and app friction reduction. We are early days, and Arlie Sisson is taking a holistic approach to digital commerce that will bring game-changing innovations.

exchanges.question: Should we expect HEAP rollout labor to be reinvested into the production line, and will it help drive traffic and customer satisfaction?
exchanges.answer: We save about two to four hours of efficiency depending on volume and leave that labor in the restaurant for morning prep and peak throughput deployment. This translates into transactions, Max 15 throughput efficiencies, total sales, and better food taste scores.

exchanges.question: Why is 350 company-operated openings per year the right level compared to the prior ceiling of 400, and what is the gating factor?
exchanges.answer: Opening one restaurant per day is meaningful growth that we can handle and support as an organization without fracturing the base. Incremental growth will also come from global expansion through partner-operated restaurants ramping quickly in markets like the Middle East.

exchanges.question: How do you see the brand being positioned in the market with a new CMO, will the For Real campaign change, and will value and quality be highlighted more?
exchanges.answer: Fernando Machado is leading the next evolution of For Real, highlighting fresh food preparation, ingredients, and our culture of cultivating a better world. We will celebrate extraordinary value based on best ingredients, fresh preparation, abundance, speed, and approachable price points.

exchanges.question: Does the 1% Q3 comp guide assume a 3% underlying trend with a sustained 2% headwind, and what is the system Max 15-minute throughput?
exchanges.answer: Yes, the 1% guide assumes the continuation of that 200 basis point impact through the rest of the quarter. HEAP restaurants do two to four extra entrees in Max 15; overall in-store is in the low 20 range, digital is mid-teens, and combined is low to mid-30s.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on in-restaurant loyalty efforts, and do in-store transactions without loyalty over-index with lower income guests?
exchanges.answer: The non-loyalty in-store transactions do not over-index with lower income guests and are broad-based. In August, we are piloting a frictionless one-stop pay where paying automatically earns rewards points without needing to scan a card or use a clunky process.

exchanges.question: Can you elaborate on new menu items coming in the months ahead, specifically center of the plate versus sides?
exchanges.answer: We expanded our culinary team to drive thoughtful menu innovation, running down center-of-the-plate items, beverage, sides, and desserts. Big ideas are going through our stage-gate process and could appear in late 2026 or 2027.

exchanges.question: Can you provide an update on trends by age and income cohorts, and if any groups are improving relative to higher income?
exchanges.answer: The younger and lower-income cohorts under the most pressure have improved the most compared to everyone else, driven by menu innovation like Chipotle Honey Chicken and promotions like Matchday BOGO. We saw our highest year-over-year gains in wallet share last quarter since 2024.

exchanges.question: What is the margin outlook beyond the current quarter regarding the gap between pricing and inflation?
exchanges.answer: In Q3, inflation is expected closer to 3% while pricing is closer to mid-2%, a much narrower gap than the first half. From Q4 forward, we expect pricing and inflation to match and that dislocation to disappear.

exchanges.question: Did you see regional divergences around the World Cup, and what did you learn from the measured pricing process?
exchanges.answer: Restaurants within 10 miles of World Cup stadiums saw a small 50 to 100 basis point benefit, but the overall quarter impact was under five basis points. The measured pricing process is working nicely, allowing us to measure resistance, adjust locally, and handle inflation dynamically.

exchanges.question: What is the LTO contribution to frequency uplift, and do protein LTOs bring in new cohorts versus existing guests?
exchanges.answer: LTOs like Chipotle Honey Chicken drive transaction increases from frequent guests coming more often and new guests. Protein LTOs bring in new customers whose lifetime value goes up materially, and we also see current customers visit more frequently with new menu options.

summary.overview: Apple reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $109.4 billion, representing a 16% increase from the prior year. Tim Cook, CEO, announced this will be his final earnings call before transitioning leadership to John Ternus, incoming CEO. The quarter was marked by significant memory cost increases and supply constraints on advanced nodes.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook, CEO, announced his upcoming departure and the transition of leadership to John Ternus, incoming CEO.
Tim Cook, CEO, stated that supply constraints on advanced nodes are driven by a demand forecast issue where iPhone and Mac are performing better than expected.
Tim Cook, CEO, noted that the company reluctantly raised prices due to exponential increases in memory pricing.
Tim Cook, CEO, highlighted overwhelmingly positive feedback from the public beta of Siri AI.
financialHighlights: Total revenue reached $109.4 billion, up 16% from a year ago.
iPhone revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $54.3 billion.
Mac revenue increased 29% year-over-year to $10.4 billion.
Services revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $30.7 billion.
Diluted earnings per share increased 29% year-over-year to $2.02.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects September quarter total company revenue growth of 9% to 11% year-over-year.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, projects September quarter iPhone revenue growth in the mid-teens year-over-year.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, anticipates September quarter gross margin between 47% and 48%.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, forecasts September quarter operating expenses of $19.1 billion to $19.4 billion.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, declared a Q4 2026 cash dividend of $0.27 per share.

qa.question: How much of the 9%-11% growth deceleration is supply constraint versus FX, and what are the constraints?
qa.answer: Foreign exchange is expected to be a sequential headwind of around 2.5 percentage points to the year-over-year total company growth rate, while the impact from supply constraints is expected to increase significantly sequentially across iPhone, Mac, and iPad.

qa.question: What are the expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and will it shorten replacement cycles?
qa.answer: Early feedback for the U.S.-only Apple Upgrade program is quite positive, and the company is excited about Siri AI feedback from the public beta, noting potential iCloud+ upgrade possibilities for heavy users.

qa.question: How much do supply constraints hit in December, and is there any possibility of broadening silicon providers like the Arizona fab to alleviate them?
qa.answer: The primary supply constraint is on advanced nodes for SoCs due to higher-than-expected iPhone and Mac demand, and while Apple sources over 100 million components from the Arizona fab, the company is not providing guidance beyond the September quarter.

qa.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs for memory, and do you aim to protect gross profit dollars or margins with pricing?
qa.answer: Apple reluctantly raised prices due to exponential memory cost increases, and the sequential change in services growth was driven by foreign exchange, the lack of a theatrical release, and some softness in mobile gaming.

qa.question: Have you seen any pull forward of demand from consumers or enterprise, and do you see AI opening up additional addressable markets?
qa.answer: It is not obvious that there has been a pull forward of demand with iPhone growing at 22% year-to-date, and the ability to run AI requests on device is a strategic competitive weapon.

unanswered.question: How much do supply constraints hit in December, and is there any possibility of broadening silicon providers like the Arizona fab to alleviate them?
unanswered.how: Tim Cook, CEO, avoided quantifying the December impact by explicitly stating they are not providing guidance beyond the September quarter.

Operating expenses revised from $18.8 billion to $19.1 billion in the June quarter to $19.1 billion to $19.4 billion in the September quarter.
whatChanged.toneShift: The tone shifted to a more cautious stance on supply and costs, with Tim Cook, CEO, describing memory pricing as a 100-year flood and Kevan Parekh, CFO, warning that supply constraints will increase significantly.

risksMentioned: Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects foreign exchange to be a sequential headwind of around 2.5 percentage points to the year-over-year total company growth rate.

Tim Cook, CEO, cited a lack of a theatrical release and softness in mobile gaming in the App Store as drivers for the sequential change in services growth.

exchanges.question: How much of the 9%-11% growth deceleration is supply constraint versus FX, and what are the constraints? Also, is seeking greater sourcing flexibility for memory about ensuring supply or preserving the value proposition?
exchanges.answer: Foreign exchange is expected to be a sequential headwind of around 2.5 percentage points to the year-over-year total company growth rate. The impact from supply constraints is expected to increase significantly sequentially, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. We expect to pay even higher memory costs in September, partially offset by carry-in inventory and lower non-memory component costs, and we are evaluating all options for supply.

exchanges.question: What are the expected adoption rates for the Apple Upgrade Program, and will it shorten replacement cycles? Also, what are the learnings from the iOS 27 public beta, and how does usage inform compute costs?
exchanges.answer: The Apple Upgrade program makes it easier for customers to get our latest products on a leasing plan, and early feedback is quite positive, though it is currently only available in the U.S. We are off the charts excited about Siri AI with overwhelmingly positive feedback from the public beta. While it is early for compute costs, we believe there will be upgrade possibilities on iCloud+ for heavy users.

exchanges.question: How much do supply constraints hit in December, and is there any possibility of broadening silicon providers like the Arizona fab to alleviate them?
exchanges.answer: The primary supply constraint is on advanced nodes for SoCs, driven by a demand forecast issue where iPhone and Mac are doing remarkably better than expected. We are not providing guidance beyond the September quarter. This is not a partner or supplier issue, but rather an incredibly strong product cycle, though we do source over 100 million components from the Arizona fab.

exchanges.question: Is it your intention to pursue multi-year LTAs for memory, and do you aim to protect gross profit dollars or margins with pricing? Also, what is driving the deceleration in services growth?
exchanges.answer: We reluctantly raised prices because we are in a 100-year flood on memory pricing with exponential increases. We look at units, revenue, and margin together rather than a mathematical formula. The sequential change in services growth was driven by foreign exchange, the lack of a theatrical release compared to last year, and some softness in mobile gaming in the App Store.

exchanges.question: Have you seen any pull forward of demand from consumers or enterprise, and do you see AI opening up additional addressable markets?
exchanges.answer: It is not obvious in the data that there has been a pull forward of demand, as iPhone has been growing at 22% year-to-date. It is too early to see the price elasticity impact on iPad and Mac. There are enormous opportunities for Apple in AI, and the ability to run requests on device is a strategic competitive weapon.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change the capital intensity of Apple, and how do you see the competitive landscape evolving with companies like OpenAI or SpaceX AI?
exchanges.answer: We use a hybrid model with both third-party cloud and our own data centers, and we have been growing our OpEx and spending more in AI. There are other COGS impacts, but also the ability for users to move up on iCloud plans. We are very focused on our plans and excited about the opportunities in this space.

exchanges.question: What are the updated thoughts on the Siri AI rollout in China and Europe, and how much of the sequential gross margin moderation is FX versus commodity costs?
exchanges.answer: We are working closely with the EU commission to offer Siri AI there, and it will be offered on Mac in the EU. In China, we received approval for original Apple Intelligence features and are working towards Siri AI. The sequential gross margin change is more than 100% explained by the change in memory costs, with FX having a minimal impact.

summary.overview: Kinsale reported second quarter 2026 results featuring a diluted operating EPS increase of 15.9% to $5.54 and an annualized operating return on equity of 24.4%. Gross written premiums decreased 5% due to heightened competition in the commercial property division, while ex-property premium growth remained positive.
keyTakeaways: Michael Kehoe, Chairman, President, and CEO, emphasized that Kinsale prioritizes underwriting profitability over top-line growth in a softening market.
Gross written premium growth excluding the commercial property division was 3.7% for the quarter and 4.8% for the first half of the year.
Stuart Winston, Chief Underwriting Officer, noted ongoing pricing pressure in commercial property from MGAs in London and traditional markets.
Salmaan Allibhai, Chief Analytics and Technology Officer, stated that operational efficiency gains from artificial intelligence could offset potential upward trends in reinsurance ceding commissions.
financialHighlights: Diluted operating earnings per share reached $5.54, up 15.9% over the second quarter of 2025.
Gross written premium declined 5% for the quarter, while net written premium decreased 1.4%.
Net earned premium grew 8.9% and net investment income rose 19.9% over the prior-year period.
The combined ratio was 75.5% for the quarter, compared to favorable prior year loss reserve development of 4.5 points and catastrophe losses of 1.3 points.
Float expanded to $3.4 billion, up from $3.1 billion at the end of 2025.

qa.question: The current year accident year loss ratio improved from 2Q 2025. Could you discuss the key factors that drove that, such as lower non-cat property losses, mix changes, or loss picks? Also, do you expect the reinsurance ceding commission rate to increase this year after renewals?
qa.answer: Losses for the quarter came in below expectations due to normal variability and mix of business, with reserves remaining as conservative as ever. Regarding reinsurance, the second quarter is a good indication going forward with a possible slight uptick in the loss ratio and commissions, while operating efficiency gains from AI could offset it.

qa.question: How much are ROEs compressing in E&S casualty given the segment is softening, and how are you thinking about broker commissions on a go-forward basis in a softer market?
qa.answer: We manage everything to a 20% ROE or greater, with most product lines running ahead of that and the company generating a 24.4% ROE for the quarter. Brokers maximize economics, and while soft market pricing creates normal tension, Kinsale's unmatched customer service and broad risk appetite continue to drive growth.

qa.question: Does Kinsale view 2Q as the trough for commercial property pricing, and what is driving the 3.7% growth figure excluding large account property?
qa.answer: There is still heavy pressure from MGAs in London and traditional markets on shared and layered deals, and pricing remains competitive. The growth in other lines is driven by pockets of opportunity, though some long-tail lines and construction are seeing increased competition.

qa.question: How much of the increase in inbound accounts is coming from broker engagement versus competitive pricing, and what is your current view of social inflation and casualty loss trends?
qa.answer: The increase is due to both our idle broker initiative reengaging brokers and stable hit ratios with more submissions binding. For casualty loss trends, mid-single digit increases are typical, and due to smaller accounts and lower limits, Kinsale has minimal exposure to social inflation.

summary.overview: Deere reported fiscal third quarter 2026 net sales and revenues of $12.608 billion, up 5%, alongside net income attributable to Deere & Company of $1.379 billion and diluted EPS of $5.10. Factory production output exceeded expectations, and order books are effectively full for the year.
keyTakeaways: Production & Precision Ag and Construction & Forestry are experiencing modest underproduction of a couple percentage points due to South American cautions and strong order pacing in C&F.
Early order programs for U.S. planters and sprayers are up mid-single digits, supported by strong technology take rates including doubled See & Spray adoption.
Construction & Forestry order trends remain positive with four to five months of orders on hand, supported by infrastructure projects, data centers, and rental fleets.
Direct tariff expectations for fiscal 2026 improved from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion due to Section 232 tariff changes dropping from roughly 25% to 15% on imported goods effective June 1st.
financialHighlights: Net sales and revenues reached $12.608 billion, up 5% compared to the prior period.
Equipment operations net sales totaled $10.999 billion, up 6%.
Production & Precision Ag net sales were $3.998 billion, down 6%, with an operating margin of 13.2%.
Small Ag & Turf net sales reached $3.383 billion, up 12%, with an operating margin of 18.4%.
Construction & Forestry net sales hit $3.618 billion, up 18%, with an operating margin of 12.1%.

guidance: Production & Precision Ag net sales: down approximately 10% for full year 2026.
Production & Precision Ag operating margin: 11% to 12% for full year 2026.
Small Ag & Turf net sales: up approximately 15% for full year 2026.
Small Ag & Turf operating margin: 14.5% to 15.5% for full year 2026.
Construction & Forestry net sales: up approximately 20% for full year 2026.
Construction & Forestry operating margin: 10.5% to 11.5% for full year 2026.
Worldwide Financial Services net income: $870 million for full year 2026.
Net income attributable to Deere & Company: $4.75 billion to $5 billion for full year 2026.
Effective tax rate: 24% to 26% for full year 2026.
Cash flow from equipment operations: $5 billion to $5.5 billion for full year 2026.

qa.question: How are we thinking about production versus retail by region for 2027 and what are the pricing expectations given inflationary cost pressures?
qa.answer: PPA and C&F are seeing modest underproduction of a couple percentage points this year due to South American cautions and strong order pacing. Deanna Kovar added that pricing is focused on covering inflation across EOP products and the entire PPA portfolio for 2027.

qa.question: What is drivingagogue the change in tariff expectations from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion, and what is the update on the excavator launch?
qa.answer: Direct tariffs dropped from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion mainly due to Section 232 tariff changes declining from roughly 25% to 15% on imported goods effective June 1st. Brent Norwood added that three models of Deere-designed excavators launched this spring with positive initial customer feedback, and rollouts continue over three to four years.

qa.question: Did anything slip between Q3 and Q4, and why did tractor inventory seem to build in Q3 ahead of the industry?
qa.answer: Shipment plans were largely set for the full year, and some demand was pulled ahead to manage Q4 risks with no inventory concerns. summary.overview: JPMorgan Chase reported Q2 2026 net income of $16.9 billion, or $6.14 per diluted share, delivering a 23% ROTCE. Total net interest income expectations were revised upward alongside higher revenue- and volume-driven expense projections. The firm expanded executive responsibilities across Doug and Troy as co-presidents following Marianne's planned retirement, while leadership signaled that elevated trading conditions may not persist.
keyTakeaways: The board appointed Doug and Troy as co-presidents to broaden operational management, while Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, maintained his succession timetable remains several years plus or minus.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised full-year 2026 NII ex-Markets guidance to about $96.5 billion and total NII to approximately $105.5 billion, driven by deposit balances and favorable rate dynamics.
Full-year adjusted expense expectations were lifted by $2.5 billion to about $107.5 billion, reflecting volume and incentive compensation against first-half capital markets outperformance.
CIB generated $24.9 billion in revenue, up 27% year-over-year, supported by an 86% surge in equities trading and a 30% rise in investment banking fees.
JPMorgan holds roughly $40 billion in excess capital and plans to reduce share buybacks at elevated valuations in favor of organic balance sheet deployment.
financialHighlights: Firmwide net income reached $16.9 billion with diluted EPS of $6.14, generating an ROTCE of 23%.
Firm expenses rose 15% year-over-year to $27.3 billion, matching firmwide revenue growth of 15% excluding significant items.
Credit costs totaled $2.5 billion, comprising $2.4 billion in net charge-offs and a net reserve build of $149 million.
Standardized CET1 ratio stood at 14.1%, down 20 basis points quarter-over-quarter as standardized RWA increased by $103 billion.
Asset & Wealth Management generated record client assets of $7.7 trillion, up 19% year-over-year, with long-term net inflows of $50 billion.

Jeremy Barnum, CFO, increased FY 2026 adjusted expense guidance from $105.0 billion to about $107.5 billion.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, guided the FY 2026 card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2%, improved from approximately 3.4% previously.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, announced a Q3 2026 quarterly dividend per share of $1.65.

qa.question: What led to the elevation of Doug and Troy to co-presidents, Marianne's departure, and what does it mean for Jamie Dimon's CEO tenure? Also, how sustainable is investment banking and markets strength?
qa.answer: The board elevated Doug and Troy to expand their operational leadership and prepare them for broader duties, while Marianne chose to retire once informed; Jamie Dimon stated his succession timetable is unaffected, while Jeremy Barnum noted that though equity conditions were uniquely favorable, the deal pipeline remains active.

qa.question: What is driving the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and Markets NII?
qa.answer: The $1.5 billion increase in NII ex-Markets to $96.5 billion stems from higher wholesale and consumer deposit balances, favorable deposit mix, and outperforming deposit betas against higher interest rates, while Markets NII rose to about $9 billion due to balance sheet mix and an internal $150 million equity allocation transfer.

qa.question: Can technology and AI eventually moderate expense growth to generate positive operating leverage over the next few years?
qa.answer: Jamie Dimon rejected targeting perpetual operating leverage because competitive pressure will pass AI efficiencies to clients, though expense growth could potentially slow in 2027 or 2028.

qa.question: Why characterize conditions as as good as it gets given positive dollar operating leverage, and what qualifies Troy to run consumer banking?
qa.answer: Jamie Dimon argued current asset prices and trading volumes leave limited incremental upside, while Troy's analytical intellect and cross-firm operational leadership fit the consumer banking role; Jeremy Barnum added that $1.5 billion of the $2.5 billion expense guide hike was already booked against first-half outperformance.

qa.question: Why continue buying back stock at three times tangible book value instead of preserving excess capital for deployment or M&A?
qa.answer: Jeremy Barnum stated the firm prefers organically deploying its roughly $40 billion in excess capital at a 17% return into global data centers, infrastructure, and security, and Jamie Dimon confirmed buybacks will be reduced at higher share prices while monitoring potential inorganic opportunities.

qa.question: Are tech and marketing investments being pulled forward in the expense outlook, and how significant is token expense?
qa.answer: Jeremy Barnum stated that expense increases are primarily volume- and revenue-driven, with token expenses remaining financially immaterial for the full year despite accelerating in the second half.

exchanges.question: What led to the elevation of Doug and Troy to co-presidents, Marianne's departure, and what does it mean for Jamie Dimon's CEO tenure? Also, how sustainable is the strength seen across investment banking and markets?
exchanges.answer: The board decided to make two co-presidents to prepare them to do far more, and Marianne opted to retire once she knew of the plans; it does not change the CEO succession timetable. On investment banking and markets, Barnum noted that while IB had pull-forward and large IPOs, the pipeline is robust and driving more activity; for equities, the specific combination of favorable conditions is unlikely to repeat, but client risk appetite remains strong.

exchanges.question: How are retail deposit trends tracking toward the 15% market share aspiration in a higher-for-longer rate environment? Also, where is the firm in its investment cycle and what does that imply for medium-term operating leverage?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposits beat expectations aided by lending and data centers, while consumer deposit growth remains on track for low single-digit growth for the year amid strong checking account openings offset by yield-seeking flows. The 15% retail share goal remains an expected natural long-term outcome. On investments, Dimon and Barnum stated spending is a continuation of ongoing multi-year investments in branches, bankers, and AI, which still support exceptional returns.

exchanges.question: What are the drivers of the upward revision to full-year NII ex-Markets and the expected exit run rate? What is driving the increase in markets NII guidance despite higher rate expectations?
exchanges.answer: The NII ex-Markets guidance revision from $95 billion to $96.5 billion is driven primarily by higher deposit balances across wholesale and consumer, favorable mix shift, and higher short- and long-end interest rates with outperforming consumer betas. Markets NII was raised to about $9 billion due to balance sheet mix with lower financed non-interest-bearing assets and an internal shift of about $150 million in equity allocation from corporate to CIB.

exchanges.question: What key characteristics is the board seeking in the next CEO, and should investors view Dimon's remaining tenure as fixed or rolling?
exchanges.answer: The successor must possess strong management skills, analytics, EQ, heart, grit, work ethic, and culture carrier qualities across the entire firm, including branches and call centers. The succession timetable remains essentially unchanged at several or a few years plus or minus, ultimately decided by the board.

exchanges.question: Can technology and AI eventually moderate expense growth to generate positive operating leverage over the next few years? Also, is there an update on potential regulatory changes regarding Basel III and the G-SIB surcharge?
exchanges.answer: Chasing perpetual operating leverage is misguided, as benefits from AI will largely accrue to customers through competition, though expense growth could potentially slow in 2027 or 2028. On regulation, Dimon urged regulators to remove double counting in operational and market risk capital, adjust G-SIB scores appropriately, and fix the short-term wholesale funding metric. Barnum added that removing RWA from the denominator in short-term wholesale funding unfairly penalizes universal banks relative to investment bank competitors.

exchanges.question: With performance firing on all cylinders, are results as good as they get or is it early cycle? Also, is there a tipping point where higher interest rates cause deposit betas to convexity-accelerate?
exchanges.answer: Conditions are getting close to as good as it gets, though duration is uncertain. On deposit betas, Barnum explained that historical models predicted negative convexity would have occurred by now, but it has not; nonetheless, stress models do incorporate potential acceleration in rate paid and deposit franchise repurchasing under severe rate shocks.

exchanges.question: Given that dollar operating leverage is positive and marginal margins are near 77%, why characterize the environment as as good as it gets? Also, what qualifies Troy, with an options trading background, to lead the consumer bank?
exchanges.answer: Markets are currently exuberant with high volumes and asset prices, meaning future upside may be limited. For the $2.5 billion expense guide increase, Barnum noted $1.5 billion was already booked against $6.5 billion in first-half capital markets revenue outperformance, leaving $1.0 billion for the second half. On Troy, Dimon emphasized his analytical intellect, culture carrying, and operational leadership across CIB, arguing that broad cross-firm leadership experience benefits consumer banking.

exchanges.question: Could AI enable banks to become significantly leaner and restructure operations as tech companies have done? Also, what specific factors drove the exceptional equity trading performance that may not repeat?
exchanges.answer: The firm has nearly 1,000 AI use cases with 50 primary applications in areas like risk, fraud, and marketing, and while discrete departments have seen 30% to 40% job cuts, displaced employees were mostly redeployed; long-term gains will compete away to customer benefit. On equities, Barnum cited major IPOs, index rebalancing, Asian market activity, and complex dynamics in Korean equities as unique drivers unlikely to repeat in aggregate.

exchanges.question: What trends are you seeing in consumer resilience and commercial CapEx? Why continue buying back stock at three times tangible book value instead of preserving excess capital for deployment or M&A?
exchanges.answer: Consumer spending remains robust across income tiers, delinquencies are lower than projected, and the labor market remains strong. The firm has roughly $40 billion in excess capital and prefers deploying it organically at a 17% return into massive global infrastructure, data center, and security needs rather than share repurchases; Dimon added that share buybacks will be dialled down at higher share prices while keeping an eye on inorganic adjacencies.

exchanges.question: What is the status and rollout plan for the smart cash tool? Also, what is the firm's broader consumer banking strategy across major European markets?
exchanges.answer: The smart cash tool is in testing for narrow segments competing for investment and deposit balances, with rollouts scheduled for later this year. In Europe, the firm is leveraging a digital platform model rather than branch overhead, having reached 2.5 to 3 million customers in Chase UK and expanded to Berlin, with plans to add investment products and credit cards toward building a profitable pan-European digital bank.

exchanges.question: Are competitors exhibiting irrational underwriting in credit markets, particularly in areas like data centers? Could the industry reach a period of regulatory stability that benefits bank valuations?
exchanges.answer: JPMorgan has passed on data center loans where competitors took excessive power supply, tenant, or relationship risks. Dimon cited mild competitor deterioration via aggressive revenue assumptions, expense add-backs, PIK structures, and covenant-lite terms. On regulation, Barnum supported stability where internal risk frameworks serve as true north, while Dimon criticized bureaucratic rules and resolution plans that failed in 2023, urging focus on core safety and interest rate risk.

exchanges.question: Are tech and marketing investments being pulled forward in the expense outlook, and how significant is token expense? Also, are there internal balance sheet constraints on capital allocation to the CIB?
exchanges.answer: Expense increases remain largely volume- and revenue-related; AI token expense was trivial in the first half and will accelerate in the second half but remains financially immaterial for the full year. Capital allocation in CIB expanded in response to client demand and passive market increases, supported by abundant excess capital, though banking industry reserve demand and liquidity regulations will require eventual adjustment.
