qa.question: How much of the September 9%-11% growth deceleration is supply constraints versus FX, and what are the supply constraints broadening beyond advanced SoCs?
qa.answer: Parekh said September growth reflects about 2.5 points of sequential FX headwind plus supply constraints expected to increase significantly, affecting iPhone, Mac and iPad; combined, close to June-quarter growth. Cook said June constraints were primarily Mac, less on iPhone and iPad. Parekh said memory costs will be higher in September, partly offset by carry-in inventory, and that the DRAM market has three suppliers; Apple is evaluating all options.

qa.question: What adoption rates are expected for the Apple Upgrade Program, and will Siri AI drive holiday iPhone demand?
qa.answer: Cook said Apple Upgrade makes latest products easier to get via a leasing plan with residual values much higher than competitors; uptake is yet to be seen. Parekh said it is currently available only in the U.S. Cook said there is no complete plan yet for Siri AI compute costs, expects some users to use it heavily, and plans iCloud+ upgrade tiers.

qa.question: Street models December-quarter growth decelerating to 8%-9%; how much will supply constraints hit December?
qa.answer: Cook said the primary constraint is advanced nodes for SoCs, that demand exceeded forecast for iPhone and Mac, and that supply has been pulled ahead. Parekh said the September guidance includes these dynamics and FX, with no color beyond September.

qa.question: What drives services deceleration from 16% to 12% and the implied sub-10% fiscal Q4 growth, including App Store effects?
qa.answer: Parekh said services deceleration is mainly sequential FX, with the prior-year F1 theatrical release lapped. App Store faced mobile gaming headwinds and business model changes in some countries, and the U.S. link-out ruling is being appealed to the Supreme Court; App Store still set a June-quarter record. Parekh expects about a 5 point FX headwind to year-over-year services growth from March to September quarter.

qa.question: What hurdles remain for launching Siri AI in China and Europe, and what drove the sequential gross margin moderation to the 46.5% guidance midpoint?
qa.answer: Cook said Apple is working closely with the EU Commission, launching in the EU is not yet possible, and Mac will get Siri AI there. In China, approval was received last week for original Apple Intelligence features, with more work needed for Siri AI. Parekh said the memory cost change explains more than 100% of the sequential gross margin change from 49.3% in March to 48.1% in June (adjusted), with FX a minimal factor.

unanswered.question: How much will supply constraints hit the December quarter?
unanswered.how: Parekh gave no color beyond September, deferring to the September guidance.

unanswered.question: How is memory sourcing flexibility aimed: securing supply or mitigating memory inflation and preserving customer value?

unanswered.question: Will Siri AI change Apple's capital intensity given the on-device and back-end compute mix?

summary.overview: JPMorgan's fiscal Q2 2026 results showed net income of $16.9 billion and EPS of $6.14, with revenue ex-significant items up 15% YoY and expenses up 15% YoY to $27.3 billion. Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised several full-year 2026 guidance figures, including NII ex-Markets to about $96.5 billion from $95 billion and adjusted expense to about $107.5 billion from $105 billion. Management described the current environment as strong but not repeatable at peak levels.
keyTakeaways: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, said IB fees were fine historically but not at peak, with some pull-forward and large deals boosting the quarter.
Barnum said the equities strength reflected major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean equity dynamics and Asia activity, and that such a combination seems improbable to repeat.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said it is 'getting close to as good as it gets' and that nobody knows how long it will last.
Dimon said perpetual operating leverage is not realistic and that a slowdown in expense growth may come in 2027 or 2028.
Barnum said consumer deposit growth is still expected to be low single-digit this year, unchanged, with yield-seeking flows a risk.
financialHighlights: Net income $16.9 billion and EPS $6.14, with ROTCE of 23%.
CIB revenue $24.9 billion, up 27% YoY, with IB fees up 30% and equities markets revenue up 86% YoY; fixed income markets revenue up 6% YoY.
CCB revenue $20.3 billion, up 8% YoY, with CCB net income $5.3 billion.
AWM revenue $6.9 billion, up 19% YoY, with AUM of $5.1 trillion, up 18% YoY, and long-term net inflows of $50 billion.
Credit costs $2.5 billion, with net charge-offs of $2.4 billion and a net reserve build of $149 million; standardized CET1 ratio 14.1%, down 20 basis points QoQ.
guidance: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, guides NII ex-Markets for FY2026 to about $96.5 billion, up from $95 billion.
Barnum guides total FY2026 NII to approximately $105.5 billion and Markets NII to about $9 billion.
Barnum guides FY2026 adjusted expense to about $107.5 billion, a $2.5 billion increase from the prior $105 billion.
Barnum guides FY2026 card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2%, down from 3.4%.
Barnum says the quarterly dividend will be $1.65 per share, effective third quarter 2026, and that about $40 billion of excess capital is expected to deploy over time.

qa.question: How should management changes, including Doug and Troy elevated to co-presidents, be viewed, and how sustainable is the strong IB and markets activity?
qa.answer: Dimon said the board chose two co-presidents to prepare them for more responsibility and the timetable has not changed. Barnum said IB fees were not at peak, with some pull-forward and large deals boosting the quarter, and that the pipeline remains robust.

qa.question: What drives the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and the second-half cadence, and why is Markets NII guided higher despite higher rates?
qa.answer: Barnum said the biggest driver of the NII ex-Markets revision from $95 billion to $96.5 billion is deposit balances across wholesale and consumer, with mix shift toward higher margin. Markets NII rises because of lower expected finance non-interest-bearing assets in the second half, and a roughly $150 million NII shift from the equity allocation increase to CIB is a rare non-offset item.

qa.question: Is operating leverage negative given 15% revenue growth, and what gives confidence Troy is right to run the consumer bank?
qa.answer: Barnum said the expense guide rose $2.5 billion, with $1.5 billion already booked from outperformance and $1 billion implicitly added for the second half, and that consensus had expected negative operating leverage. Dimon cited Troy's markets and IB experience and said the franchise needs leaders with experience across the company.
qa.read: Answered partially; the Troy question was answered with background rather than a specific rationale.

qa.question: What is the status and rollout of the smart cash tool, and what are the European consumer banking aspirations?
qa.answer: Dimon said the smart cash tool is a test case for a narrow segment of accounts and something will be seen this year. Chase UK has nearly 3 million customers, Berlin was opened, and Germany is ahead of plan but not yet profitable.

qa.question: Why buy back stock at about three times tangible book with excess capital?
qa.answer: Barnum said approximately $40 billion of excess capital will be deployed and that the world needs capital for many uses. Dimon said the firm is making an investment decision, has large organic opportunities, and targets a 17% return.

exchanges.question: How should management changes, including Doug and Troy elevated to co-presidents, be viewed for leadership development and CEO tenure? Also, how sustainable is the strong IB and markets activity and how risk-on are the businesses?
exchanges.answer: Dimon said the board chose two co-presidents to prepare them for more responsibility; the timetable has not changed. Marianne decided to retire rather than stay. Barnum said IB fees were fine historically but not at peak, with some pull-forward and large deals boosting the quarter. Pipeline remains robust. Equities strength is hard to repeat; the market is risk-on and the firm is a taker of that risk.

exchanges.question: What is the progression toward the 15% retail deposit market share goal and how might higher-for-longer rates affect share gains? Where are we in the expense investment cycle and its operating leverage outlook?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposit growth was strong and ahead of expectations for the first half. Consumer deposit growth still expected low single-digit this year, unchanged, with yield-seeking flows a risk. The 15% share is an outcome of the strategy, not a target. Dimon said expense investment is a continuation of past practice with no expected change. Barnum said the firm will always invest for future returns.

exchanges.question: What drives the upward revision to NII ex-Markets and the second-half cadence and exit rate? Why is markets NII guided higher despite higher rates?
exchanges.answer: NII ex-Markets revised up from $95 billion to $96.5 billion for the full year; the biggest driver is deposit balances across wholesale and consumer, with mix shift toward higher margin. Rates were higher, and consumer beta outperformance adds sensitivity. Markets NII rises because of lower expected finance non-interest-bearing assets in the second half. A roughly $150 million NII shift from the equity allocation increase to CIB is a rare non-offset item.

exchanges.question: What characteristics is the board seeking in the next CEO, and is the succession timetable fixed or a rolling retirement with executive chair role?
exchanges.answer: Dimon listed leadership traits and said the timing is essentially the same and up to the board. He cited the co-presidents, Jen Piepszak as COO, and Mary Erdoes running AWM. He said the timetable is several years, plus or minus, and the decision is up to the board.

exchanges.question: Is there a time over the intermediate term when expense growth could slow so operating leverage becomes more likely, given AI and technology benefits?
exchanges.answer: Dimon said perpetual operating leverage is not realistic and that AI benefits will largely accrue to customers. He said a slowdown in expense growth may come in 2027 or 2028. Investment opportunities will be pursued when they earn good returns. He also raised the regulatory question.

exchanges.question: Is this as good as it gets, or are we early cycle? Is there a tipping point where deposit behavior and betas change as rates rise?
exchanges.answer: Dimon said it is getting close to as good as it gets and nobody knows how long it lasts. Barnum said the firm does not know the tipping point but negative convexity in consumer deposit rate paid should eventually appear. It is modeled in stress tests. Dimon said some of that is assumed in the models.

exchanges.question: Is operating leverage negative given 15% revenue growth? What gives confidence Troy is right to run the consumer bank?
exchanges.answer: Barnum said the expense guide rose $2.5 billion, with $1.5 billion already booked from outperformance and $1 billion implicitly added for second half. Consensus had expected negative operating leverage. Dimon said the environment is healthy but duration is unknown. On Troy, Dimon cited his markets and IB experience and that the franchise needs leaders with experience across the company.

exchanges.question: Are AI efficiency benefits being underestimated, could banks run leaner structures? What was most exceptional in equities this quarter that may not repeat?
exchanges.answer: Dimon said AI will produce efficiency in parts of the company, with almost 1,000 use cases and around 50 important ones. Some job reductions of 30% or 40% occurred with most people reassigned. Benefits will accrue to customers. Barnum said the equities strength reflected major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean equity dynamics and Asia activity, and such a combination seems improbable to repeat.

exchanges.question: What is the consumer resilience and CapEx breadth beyond AI? Why buy back stock at about three times tangible book with excess capital?
exchanges.answer: Barnum said CapEx lending is broad but may be AI-related in non-obvious places. Consumer spend is robust, delinquencies are lower than expected, and K-shape narrative is not supported. Buybacks: approximately $40 billion of excess capital deployment; the world needs capital for many uses. Dimon said the firm is making an investment decision, has large organic opportunities, and targets a 17% return.

exchanges.question: What is the status and rollout of the smart cash tool, and what are the European consumer banking aspirations?
exchanges.answer: Dimon said the smart cash tool is a test case for a narrow segment of accounts and something will be seen this year. For Europe, Chase UK has nearly 3 million customers and Berlin was opened, with Germany ahead of plan but not yet profitable. Investment products were added in the UK, with cards possibly next. The aspiration is a pan-European digital bank.

exchanges.question: What are you seeing in competitors' credit underwriting? Could regulatory stability enhance bank valuations?
exchanges.answer: Barnum said data center underwriting shows competitive pressure, with the firm passing on some deals. Dimon described a mild weakening in underwriting across revenue assumptions, PIK, covenants and rollover risk, concentrated in some players. Barnum said regulatory stability is desirable but he is not convinced it drives bank valuations. Dimon argued for clearer legislation and a safety-and-soundness focus.

exchanges.question: Are other expense categories being raised, such as tech or marketing pull-forward? How nimble is CIB capital allocation and are there internal limits?
exchanges.answer: Barnum said some other categories are moving, with marketing partly undisclosed. Token expense is trivial in the first half but forecast to accelerate meaningfully in the second half, with full-year impact still trivial and largely budgeted. CIB capital allocation reflects client demand plus passive effects. Liquidity is tighter at the margin, and liquidity regulation is the next agenda item. Dimon said risk standards have not changed.

exchanges.question: What is the status and rollout timing of the smart cash tool? What are your European consumer banking aspirations?

exchanges.question: What are you seeing in competitors' credit underwriting? Could the regulatory environment reach stability that lifts bank valuations?

Dimon said mild weakening: aggressive revenue assumptions, expense add-backs, more PIK, weaker covenants, rollover risk; outliers will emerge in a credit cycle. On regulation, stability is desirable; Barnum unconvinced regulation is a major valuation drag; Dimon welcomed a step back by Bowman and Warsh.

exchanges.answer: Some ups and downs but volume and revenue-related expense is the main driver. summary.overview: Apple's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $109.4B, up 16% YoY and a June quarter record, with iPhone up 22% to $54.3B, Mac up 29% to $10.4B and diluted EPS of $2.02, up 29% including an $0.11 tariff refund benefit. Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided September quarter revenue growth to 9%-11%, citing a ~2.5pt sequential FX headwind and supply constraints that increase significantly across iPhone, Mac and iPad. Tim Cook, CEO, said this was his final earnings call, with John Ternus leading future calls.
keyTakeaways: Tim Cook, CEO, said the primary constraint is advanced-node SoC availability and called the root cause a demand forecast issue rather than a supply issue, with September a 'scrambling' quarter.
Tim Cook, CEO, said Apple reluctantly raised prices on iPad and Mac due to a '100-year flood' in memory pricing, and that it is too early to judge elasticity.

Kevan Parekh, CFO, said services growth slowed from 16% in Q2 to 12%, driven mainly by FX, the year-ago F1 theatrical compare, mobile gaming softness, App Store model changes and the U.S. link-out ruling.
Tim Cook, CEO, said Siri AI public beta feedback is overwhelmingly positive, but the plan for compute costs is early and not complete, with iCloud+ upgrade tiers planned for heavy users.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, declined to provide any color beyond the September quarter.
financialHighlights: Revenue $109.4B, up 16% YoY; products $78.7B, up 18%; services $30.7B, up 12%, a June quarter record.
iPhone $54.3B, up 22%; Mac $10.4B, up 29%; iPad $6.2B, down 6%; wearables $7.9B, up 6%.
Gross margin 50.1%, up 80bp sequentially with ~2pt tariff refund benefit; 48.1% ex-refund vs 49.3% in March, a 120bp decline Kevan Parekh, CFO, said was more than 100% explained by memory costs.
Operating expenses $19.1B, up 23% YoY on R&D; net income $29.8B and operating cash flow $34.4B, both June quarter records.
Capital return of $33B ($4B dividends, $25.8B buybacks); cash and marketable securities $147B against $84B debt.
guidance: Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided September quarter revenue growth of 9%-11% YoY, including a ~2.5pt sequential FX headwind, versus the prior June guide of 14%-17%.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, expects iPhone revenue growth in the mid-teens and services growth largely similar to June's 12% after removing a ~2.5pt sequential FX headwind.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided gross margin of 47%-48% including ~1pt tariff refund benefit (46.5% midpoint ex-refund, down 160bp from June ex-refund), versus 47.5%-48.5% guided for June.
Kevan Parekh, CFO, guided OpEx of $19.1B-$19.4B (prior $18.8B-$19.1B), OI&E around $350M (prior ~$250M) and a tax rate around 16.5% (prior ~17%).
Tim Cook, CEO, said memory costs will be even higher in September than June, with carry-in inventory offsets decreasing beyond September and market pricing continuing to rise.

qa.question: How much of the ~500bp deceleration implied by the 9%-11% guide is supply versus FX, and are memory sourcing options about supply or customer value?
qa.answer: The guide reflects a ~2.5pt sequential FX headwind plus supply constraints increasing significantly across iPhone, Mac and iPad; combining both gets close to June's growth rate. Tim Cook, CEO, added that memory costs were significantly higher in June than March, higher still in September with partial carry-in inventory offset that declines afterward, and that DRAM has three suppliers with Apple evaluating all options.

qa.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter, and could Apple broaden silicon providers such as the Arizona fab?
qa.answer: Cook pushed back that the root cause is a demand forecast issue, not a supply or partner issue, with iPhone up 22% and Mac up 29%; supply has been pulled ahead and September will be a scrambling quarter. Apple sources over 100 million components from Arizona this year under its $600B U.S. commitment. Kevan Parekh, CFO, gave no color beyond September.

qa.question: Will Apple pursue multi-year supplier LTAs, is pricing meant to protect gross profit dollars or margin percent, and why did services growth of 12% miss and decelerate further?
qa.answer: Cook said prices were raised reluctantly amid exponential memory increases and pricing weighs units, revenue and margin over the long term, not a formula; LTAs were not addressed. Kevan Parekh, CFO, attributed the 16% to 12% decel to FX, the F1 theatrical compare, mobile gaming softness, App Store model changes and the U.S. link-out ruling, with FX a ~5pt headwind March to September and another 2.5pt June to September.

qa.question: Status of Siri AI in China and Europe, and the FX versus commodity split in the gross margin decline from 48% ex-refund to the 46.5% midpoint?
qa.answer: Siri AI is not yet enabled in the EU for iPhone/iPad but is or will be on Mac; China approved original Apple Intelligence features last week, with more work needed for Siri AI. Kevan Parekh, CFO, said the 160bp June-to-September ex-refund decline is more than explained by memory, partly offset by carry-in inventory, lower non-memory costs and mix, with FX minimal.

qa.question: Will Siri AI change capital intensity, and how is the competitive landscape evolving with OpenAI or SpaceX AI potentially building devices?
qa.answer: Apple runs a hybrid of third-party cloud and own data centers; AI spend sits in both OpEx and COGS, and the net cost impact of Siri AI, offset by iCloud plan upgrades, remains uncertain. John Ternus, Incoming CEO, said Apple is focused on its own plans.

unanswered.question: How much supply constraints affect the December quarter.
unanswered.how: Kevan Parekh, CFO, said no color is being provided beyond September.

unanswered.question: How Siri AI usage informs compute costs and recovery via iCloud+.

exchanges.question: How much of the ~500bp deceleration implied by the 9%-11% September guide is supply constraint vs FX, and what are the constraints broadening beyond advanced SoCs? Second, are memory sourcing options about securing supply/mitigating inflation or preserving customer value proposition?
exchanges.answer: September guide of 9%-11% reflects ~2.5pt sequential FX headwind to YoY growth plus supply constraints increasing significantly sequentially across iPhone, Mac and iPad; combining both gets close to June's growth rate. June constraints were primarily Mac, lesser on iPhone/iPad, driven by very high demand and availability of advanced nodes for SoCs, with less supply chain flexibility than normal. On memory: paid significantly more in June than March, partly offset by carry-in inventory; September memory costs even higher, partly offset by carry-in inventory (benefit decreasing beyond September) and lower non-memory component costs; beyond September market memory pricing continues to increase. DRAM has three suppliers; more would help on supply side, unclear on pricing; evaluating all options.

exchanges.question: Expected adoption of Apple Upgrade across the 2.5B install base and whether it shortens iPhone replacement cycles or equally helps Mac/iPad? Second, learnings from iOS 27/Siri AI public beta, whether it drives holiday iPhone demand, and how usage informs compute costs and recovery via iCloud+?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade is a leasing plan leveraging higher residual values of Apple products; offered in retail stores, not widely in all channels, U.S. only; early feedback quite positive but uptake to be seen. Siri AI developer beta released immediately after WWDC keynote, public beta a few weeks ago, feedback overwhelmingly positive. Compute cost plan is early and not complete; will offer iCloud+ upgrade tiers for heavy users.

exchanges.question: How much do supply constraints hit the December quarter given Street at 8%-9% growth? Also, could Apple broaden silicon providers (e.g., Arizona fab) in a reasonable timeframe to alleviate constraints?
exchanges.answer: Primary constraint is advanced nodes for SoCs; root cause is a demand forecast issue, not a supply issue, with iPhone up 22% (also 22% year-to-date) and Mac up 29%; supply has been pulled ahead and there is a limit, so September will be a scrambling quarter. Kevan: 9%-11% guidance built on these dynamics plus FX; no color or guidance beyond September. Not a partner/supplier issue; Apple sources over 100 million components this year from Arizona as part of the $600 billion U.S. commitment and is pleased with that fab's ramp.

exchanges.question: Will Apple pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers, and in pricing is the intent to protect gross profit dollars or gross margin percentage? Second, why did services growth of 12% fall below guidance and what drives the further deceleration implied for Q4, including App Store/mobile gaming and AI impact?
exchanges.answer: Prices were raised reluctantly due to a '100-year flood' in memory pricing with exponential increases; pricing considers units, revenue and margin together over the long term, not a formula. Kevan: services decel from 16% in Q2 to 12% driven mainly by FX, plus year-ago F1 theatrical release benefit (also affects September compare), mobile gaming headwinds, App Store business model changes in certain countries and U.S. court ruling on link-outs (Supreme Court will hear appeal); App Store still set June quarter record. Roughly met expectations except more mobile gaming softness. FX is about a 5pt headwind to services growth from March to September, with another 2.5pt sequential headwind from June to September.

exchanges.question: Has Apple seen any pull-forward of demand from consumers, enterprise or education ahead of memory-driven price increases? Second, does AI open additional addressable markets over time?
exchanges.answer: iPhone has run at 22% growth year to date and pull-forward is not obvious in the data; prices were raised on iPad and Mac and it is too early to judge elasticity given channel inventory and consumer response lag, with more understanding in the weeks ahead. Sees enormous AI opportunities; running a percentage of requests on device is strategic and a competitive weapon.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change Apple's capital intensity given hybrid on-device, first-party and third-party cloud? Second, for John Ternus, how is the competitive landscape evolving with OpenAI or SpaceX AI potentially building devices?
exchanges.answer: Apple uses a hybrid model of third-party cloud and own data centers; OpEx has grown with substantially more AI spend, and AI costs also sit in COGS; cost impact of Siri AI remains to be seen, with offset from users moving up iCloud plans; balance uncertain. Ternus: lots of opportunity in the space, Apple is focused on its plans and very excited.

exchanges.question: Update on launching Siri AI in China and Europe and hurdles remaining? Second, walk through sequential gross margin decline from 48% ex-tariff refund to 46.5% guided midpoint: FX vs commodity costs?
exchanges.answer: Working closely with the EU commission; Siri AI not yet enabled in the EU for iPhone/iPad but is or will be offered on Mac there since Mac is not covered by the same regulations. China: last week received approval to ship original Apple Intelligence features like cleanup; rolling out now, more work required for Siri AI. Kevan: March to June gross margin fell 120bp (49.3% to 48.1% ex-refund), more than 100% explained by memory cost; June to September 160bp decline (48.1% to 46.5% midpoint ex-refund) also more than explained by memory, with partial offsets from carry-in inventory, lower non-memory component costs and favorable mix; FX minimal.

summary.overview: Lilly's Q2 2026 call reported revenue up 48% versus Q2 2025, with U.S. revenue up 33% driven by volume and U.S. price down 3%. Lilly raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $85 billion to $87 billion, and Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, said "we're not satisfied" when closing on progress this year. Q&A centred on the Foundayo launch curve, Medicare Bridge uptake, retatrutide's BLA pathway and pricing.
keyTakeaways: Lucas Montarce, CFO, raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $85 billion to $87 billion, with the low end up $3 billion and the high end up $2 billion.
Ilya Yuffa, President of Lilly USA, said the Foundayo U.S. launch reached an inflection in the last week of July, with volume almost doubling versus a month earlier.
Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, said Lilly needs more CMC work before retatrutide's BLA and targets submission in Q1 2027.
Lucas Montarce, CFO, said Q2 pre-period U.S. rebate and discount estimate adjustments will not continue into the second half.
Dan Skovronsky, Chief Scientific and Product Officer, said Lilly's pipeline would be a "really strong and large pipeline" even without incretins.
financialHighlights: Revenue grew 48% versus Q2 2025; key products increased almost $6.8 billion.
Non-GAAP performance margin was 54.8%, up 9 percentage points versus Q2 2025.
Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 including a $3.03 acquired IPR&D charge, versus $6.31 in Q2 2025 including $0.14.
MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND revenue reached $14.9 billion, contributing $6.3 billion of growth versus Q2 2025.
Marketing, selling and administrative expenses rose 25% and R&D expenses rose 14% versus Q2 2025.

Lucas Montarce, CFO, guides full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS to $35.50 to $36.50, before updating for the $3.03 Q2 acquired IPR&D charge; prior was $35.50 to $37.
Dan Skovronsky, CSPO, expects the retatrutide U.S. BLA submission in Q1 2027.
Dave Ricks, CEO, expects Foundayo Type 2 diabetes U.S. regulatory action later this year and says Medicare Bridge eligibility expands to 20 million eligible Americans from July 1, 2026.

qa.question: Reasons for the slower-than-anticipated U.S. Foundayo launch curve and when an inflection is expected.
qa.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
qa.answer: Yuffa cited physician education, access and affordability, and consumer awareness as focus areas; CVS added Foundayo in June. The last week of July showed inflection with volume almost doubling versus a month earlier, and around one in four new starts are on Foundayo.

qa.question: Requirements and milestones to get retatrutide accepted as a BLA.
qa.answer: Lilly has all clinical data needed but needs more CMC work, is in communication with the FDA, and will update on filing status. Submission is targeted for Q1 next year, and the court decision on biologic status is mixed with active litigation.

qa.question: Whether guidance implies a second-half revenue deceleration versus Q2.
qa.answer: Pre-period U.S. rebate and discount estimate adjustments this quarter will not continue into the second half. The 2025 base included a bolus of second-half MOUNJARO launches in new U.S. markets that will not recur, and Europe Q3 and U.S. Type 2 diabetes Q4 seasonality are factored into guidance.

qa.question: Sustainability of net pricing on obesity given medical exceptions and the CVS formulary return.
qa.answer: ZEPBOUND prices range from $299 to $449 on LillyDirect and $245 under Bridge. Medical exceptions are a short-term driver, the CVS access agreement starts in Q4, and price decline is embedded in guidance and more than offset by volume growth.

qa.question: Whether psychiatry and vaccines are scalable priority areas or one-off deals.
qa.responderTitle: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
qa.answer: Van Naarden said both areas share immense unmet need and the deals offer impactful technology at disciplined prices. He declined to forward-look on further infectious disease or psychiatry deals, saying Lilly will be opportunistic.

exchanges.question: How Lilly is expanding the consumer treatment opportunity, and how U.S. versus international self-pay markets compare.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa said mid-single-digit obesity treatment penetration leaves significant opportunity; Bridge and some state Medicaid access are improving access; obesity TRxs were about 3 million; about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay. Jonsson said OUS obesity is mainly out-of-pocket, Lilly has launched LillyDirect versions outside the U.S., and regulations differ by market.

exchanges.question: Reasons for slower-than-anticipated U.S. Foundayo launch curve and when an inflection is expected; OUS competitive dynamics versus Novo Nordisk oral launches.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa cited physician education, access and affordability, and consumer awareness as focus areas; CVS added Foundayo in June; the last week of July showed inflection with volume almost doubling versus a month earlier; around one in four new starts are on Foundayo. Jonsson said UAE launched early May, most launches come in 2027, Lilly's combined incretin share held steady, and sell-in data is noisy.

exchanges.question: Requirements and milestones to get retatrutide accepted as a BLA, and whether other incretins could be classified as BLAs.
exchanges.answer: Ricks said Lilly believes retatrutide is a biologic application and there is a mixed court decision with active litigation. Lilly has all clinical data needed but needs more CMC work; it is in communication with the FDA and will update on filing status. Submission is targeted for Q1 next year.

exchanges.question: Early learnings and ramp curve from the Medicare obesity rollout, including orals versus injectables.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa said Bridge increases access for about 35% more Americans, with prior authorization and approvals working well and LillyDirect enabled to fulfill Bridge. Inflection seen over recent weeks for ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO. About 80% of treated patients are on injectable; roughly 60-70% of new people had no prior access.

exchanges.question: Whether a commercial strategy is needed for retatrutide against currently available products, and whether retatrutide's efficacy opens additional indications.
exchanges.answer: Custer expects patients to embrace retatrutide once launched. High-dose weight loss opens additional opportunities, including knee osteoarthritis pain reduction of 75% in TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1, a MASH/MASLD study, and a chronic lower back pain study reading out next year. Lilly is evaluating more indications internally.

exchanges.question: Breast cancer strategy after Verzenio, including whether an all-oral combination is planned.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Van Naarden said Lilly has targeted medicines for estrogen receptor, CDK4/6 and PI3K alpha and plans to combine them. INLURIYO is in the EMBER-4 adjuvant trial with readout next year. Lilly is on the precipice of phase III for tersolisib, initially combined with endocrine therapies and over time with INLURIYO, with an all-oral combination envisioned in future settings.

exchanges.question: Whether guidance implies a second-half revenue deceleration versus Q2, given Medicare Bridge and Foundayo ramp; whether price or conservatism explains it.
exchanges.answer: Montarce said pre-period rebate and discount estimate adjustments in the U.S. this quarter will not continue into the second half. The 2025 base included a bolus of MOUNJARO launches in new U.S. markets in the second half, which will not recur; future growth is driven by OUS penetration. Europe seasonality in Q3 and U.S. Type 2 diabetes seasonality in Q4 are factored into guidance.

exchanges.question: Which OUS regions are growing most for MOUNJARO, and what is seen in India given generic launches and capacity constraints.
exchanges.answer: Jonsson said MOUNJARO performs strongly across most markets, with China NRDL category leadership after 16 months and significant growth in Korea, the U.K., Mexico and Germany. TRx continued growing after generic semaglutide launched in India and Brazil; Canada tirzepatide TRx growing in line with the total market. Generic companies show supply constraints, which Lilly will monitor.

exchanges.question: Extent of Foundayo sampling and whether it dampens IQVIA prescription data; U.S. prescribing base expansion.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa said Foundayo promotion uses every lever, including sampling of the first 30 days of the first dose, with full supply. Prescribers grew from 8,000 at the last earnings call to 36,000, with week-on-week progress in adoption and awareness.

exchanges.question: Sustainability of net pricing on obesity given medical exceptions and CVS formulary return, and whether this drives favorable rebate adjustments.
exchanges.answer: Montarce said ZEPBOUND prices range from $299 to $449 on LillyDirect and $245 under Bridge, with commercial prices also a factor. Medical exceptions are a driver and a short-term item; the CVS access agreement starts in Q4. Price is expected to decline, which is embedded in guidance and more than offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Whether psychiatry and vaccines are scalable priority areas for Lilly or one-off deals.
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Van Naarden said both areas share immense unmet need, and the deals offer impactful technology at disciplined prices, similar to other deals this year. He declined to forward-look on further infectious disease or psychiatry deals, saying Lilly will be opportunistic.

exchanges.question: Specific non-obesity pipeline assets the street should focus on.
exchanges.answer: Skovronsky highlighted gene editing for PCSK9, oral and injectable Lp(a)-lowering drugs, sleep-wake disorders with Centessa, and oncology readouts described as possibly the richest period ever. Also cited Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma, AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor, empagliflozin in immunology, and IBD and psoriatic disease combinations. He said the pipeline is strong even without incretins.

exchanges.question: Ex-U.S. Foundayo obesity potential given UAE sales, and whether ex-U.S. governments will reimburse Foundayo for diabetes more readily than tirzepatide.
exchanges.answer: Jonsson said UAE start is encouraging but early, with inventory build and noisy data. Majority of patients are incretin-naive, and the major OUS rollout starts in early 2027. Lilly is probably slightly better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement with an oral, given three head-to-head orforglipron trials, but reimbursement takes time and launch focus is chronic weight management.

summary.overview: JPMorgan reported Q2 2026 net income of $16.9B, EPS of $6.14 and a 23% ROTCE, with revenue ex significant items up 15% and expenses up 15% to $27.3B. CIB revenue rose 27% to $24.9B on IB fees up 30% and equities markets up 86%. Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised FY2026 NII ex-Markets guidance to ~$96.5B and adjusted expense guidance to ~$107.5B.
keyTakeaways: Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said the board named co-presidents Doug and Troy and that his succession timetable is unchanged at several years, plus or minus.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, called the equities quarter hard to imagine repeating, citing major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean equity dynamics and Asia activity.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said conditions are getting close to as good as it gets, with duration unknown.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, tied the $2.5B expense raise to $6.5B of 1H capital markets outperformance, which carried $1.5B of expense, with ~$1B implied for 2H.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said excess capital of about $40B is expected to be deployed and called his prior $20B buyback mention a mistake.
financialHighlights: Net income was $16.9B, EPS $6.14 and ROTCE 23%.
CCB earned $5.3B on revenue of $20.3B, up 8% YoY, with more than 500,000 net new checking accounts.
CIB earned $9.7B on revenue of $24.9B, up 27%, with fixed income markets up 6% and equities markets up 86%.
AWM earned $2B on revenue of $6.9B, up 19%, with a 38% pretax margin, $50B of long-term net inflows and AUM of $5.1T, up 18%.
Credit costs were $2.5B, comprising $2.4B of NCOs and a $149M reserve build, and standardized CET1 fell 20bp to 14.1% as RWA rose ~$103B.
guidance: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised FY2026 NII ex-Markets guidance to ~$96.5B from $95B, with total NII ~$105.5B and Markets NII ~$9B.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised FY2026 adjusted expense guidance to ~$107.5B from ~$105B.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, guided the FY2026 card net charge-off rate to ~3.2% and announced a $1.65/share quarterly dividend effective 3Q26.
Jeremy Barnum, CFO, kept consumer deposit growth expectations at low single digits.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, sees a possible slowdown in expense growth in 2027 or 2028 and expects something from the smart cash tool this year.

qa.question: Asked what drove the NII ex-Markets raise and why Markets NII rose despite higher rates.
qa.answer: He said the raise to $96.5B from $95B was driven mainly by deposit balances and mix, with actual rate sensitivity above EAR due to consumer beta outperformance, and that a higher CIB equity allocation shifts ~$150M into Markets NII, not offset in NIR.

qa.question: Challenged the 'as good as it gets' view and asked about Troy running consumer without consumer experience.

summary.overview: Lilly's Q2 2026 revenue rose 48% versus Q2 2025, with MOUNJARO plus ZEPBOUND at $14.9B, up $6.3B. Lucas Montarce, CFO, raised full-year revenue guidance to $85B-$87B and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50-$36.50. Dave Ricks, Chair and CEO, said "While we're pleased with the progress this year so far, we're not satisfied."
keyTakeaways: Ilya Yuffa, President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities, said U.S. Foundayo volume in the last week of July was almost double that of a month earlier, with about one in four new starts on Foundayo.
Foundayo prescribers grew from 8,000 at last earnings to 36,000, per Yuffa.
Dan Skovronsky, Chief Scientific and Product Officer, targets a retatrutide U.S. BLA submission in Q1 2027.
Lilly's global incretin share was about 55%, up about 2 points from Q1 2026.
Montarce said CVS access starting in Q4 likely shortens the medical exception effect, and that lower price is embedded in guidance.
financialHighlights: Revenue grew 48% versus Q2 2025; MOUNJARO plus ZEPBOUND revenue was $14.9B, up $6.3B.
Gross margin was 86.3%, up 1.3 points; non-GAAP performance margin was 54.8%, up 9 points.
Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 versus $6.31, including $3.03 of IPR&D.
U.S. revenue grew 33% with price down 3%, or down 9% excluding rebate estimate changes.
Europe grew 55% at CER including a $250M Jardiance milestone; China grew 93%, Japan 30% and rest of world 136%, all at CER.
guidance: Montarce guides full-year 2026 revenue to $85B-$87B, with the low end raised $3B and the high end $2B.
Montarce guides non-GAAP performance margin to 49%-50.5%, up 2 points at both the low and high end.
Montarce guides non-GAAP EPS to $35.50-$36.50, up $2.78 at the midpoint before the $3.03 Q2 IPR&D charge.
Skovronsky targets the retatrutide U.S. BLA in Q1 2027; Ricks expects Foundayo type 2 diabetes U.S. regulatory action later in 2026; Montarce expects Foundayo in all major markets in 2027.

exchanges.question: How do you see the consumer/self-pay obesity market evolving, and how similar are the U.S. and international self-pay markets?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Obesity treatment penetration is still mid-single-digit, leaving big opportunity. Access is improving via Bridge and state Medicaid; about 55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions are self-pay; Lilly is investing in consumer awareness and LillyDirect. Jonsson: OUS obesity is still mainly out of pocket, LillyDirect versions have launched outside the U.S., models differ by regulation, and Lilly is focused on safe, authentic medicines.

exchanges.question: Why has the U.S. Foundayo launch been slower than expected and when will it inflect? Also, what are competitive dynamics OUS now that Novo's oral is launching, including in the UAE?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa: focus on physician education, access/affordability, consumer awareness; CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1, DTC began. Last week of July showed inflection, with volume almost double a month ago and about one in four new starts on Foundayo. Jonsson: UAE launched early May; Lilly combined incretin share held steady with a second oral entering; most launches in 2027, no supply gating; early data are noisy and Novo data is likely sell-in.

exchanges.question: What are the requirements and milestones to get retatrutide accepted as a BLA, and would this apply to later incretins?
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes retatrutide is a biologic by amino acid count rule and protein analogy. There was a mixed first court decision and litigation is active; Lilly hopes to conclude with FDA. Lilly has all the clinical data but needs a bit more CMC data; submission targeted by Q1 next year. Did not address whether later incretins would qualify.

exchanges.question: What are the learnings from the Medicare obesity rollout, the ramp, and orals versus injectables?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Early but an inflection over the last few weeks for ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO. Prior authorization process working well; LillyDirect enabled to fulfill Bridge. About 80% of treated are injectable; approximately 60%-70% are new people without prior access.

exchanges.question: Do you need a commercial strategy to counter unauthorized retatrutide available today? Does retatrutide's higher efficacy open indications beyond those for tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: Expects people to choose authentic retatrutide once available. Retatrutide opens more opportunities: knee osteoarthritis pain reduced 75% (TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1), MASH/MASLD study ongoing, chronic lower back pain study reading out next year, other indications under evaluation.

exchanges.question: What is the post-Verzenio breast cancer strategy, and is an all-oral combination planned with the SERD and PI3K?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Lilly sees ER, CDK4/6 and PI3K alpha as key targets and has medicines for each, with plans to combine them. EMBER-4 adjuvant for INLURIYO reads out next year. Tersolisib phase III is about to start, initially with endocrine therapy and eventually with INLURIYO; the study allows investigator's choice of CDK4/6, likely Verzenio.

exchanges.question: Guidance seems to imply H2 revenue deceleration versus Q2 despite Bridge and Foundayo access; is something missing on price or is it conservatism?
exchanges.answer: Prior-period rebate/discount estimate adjustments are not expected to continue in H2. H2 2025 base had the bolus of MOUNJARO launches in new countries, and future growth is driven by OUS penetration. Dollar growth expected to stay significant; guide factors Q3 Europe vacation seasonality and Q4 U.S. type 2 diabetes seasonality. Cited a $2.5 billion guide upgrade.

exchanges.question: Which regions drive OUS growth and what are you seeing in India with generic semaglutide launching and capacity constraints?
exchanges.answer: MOUNJARO strong nearly everywhere; China NRDL gave category leadership after 16 months; growth in Korea, U.K., Mexico, Germany. In India and Brazil MOUNJARO TRx keep growing after generic semaglutide launch, helped by superiority data. In Canada tirzepatide TRx grow at the market pace; generic companies have significant supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is the Foundayo sampling program and is it dampening IQVIA scripts? How has the prescriber base expanded?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Sampling covers the first 30 days of first dose, extensive across prescribers, with full supply. Did not say whether it dampens IQVIA data. Prescribers grew from 8,000 at last earnings to 36,000.

exchanges.question: Obesity net price is well above cash prices; how sustainable is the medical exception effect given CVS is back on formulary, and does it drive favorable rebate adjustments?
exchanges.answer: Cited price points: LillyDirect $299 to $449, Bridge $245. Medical exception and script size drive price. CVS access starting in Q4 means medical exception is likely short-term; price expected to go down, embedded in guide, and more than offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines areas Lilly can scale and high priority, or one-off assets?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Common thread is large unmet need, with deals at prices allowing discipline. Not different from other deals this year. Declined to forecast further infectious disease or psychiatry build; will be opportunistic.

exchanges.question: Which one or two non-obesity pipeline assets should the Street pay more attention to?
exchanges.answer: Highlighted PCSK9 gene editing and oral and injectable Lp(a) drugs; psychiatry, vaccines and sleep-wake (Centessa) in neuroscience; Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma and AJ1-11095 in oncology; immunology progress and IBD/psoriatic combinations. Calls it the strongest pipeline ever.

exchanges.question: UAE Foundayo sales were $31M versus $67M in U.S.; how big is OUS obesity potential, and will governments reimburse it for diabetes better than tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: Encouraged but very early, with noise and initial inventory build. Most patients are incretin-naive; major OUS rollout begins early 2027. Lilly is probably slightly better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement with an oral, but reimbursement takes time; launch focus is chronic weight management.

summary.overview: Chipotle's fiscal Q2 2026 revenue reached $3.3 billion, up 9.3% year-over-year, with comparable restaurant sales of +2.2%. Restaurant level margin fell 220 basis points to 25.2% and adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.33. Adam Rymer, CFO, guided Q3 comps to around plus 1%, assuming a roughly 200 basis point Cyclospora-related impact persists, and the prior quarter's comps were +0.5%.
keyTakeaways: Scott Boatwright, CEO, said Q2 transaction growth reflected early Recipe for Growth benefits, with green shoots expected to build through the second half of 2026 and into 2027.

Adam Rymer, CFO, said traffic improved through Q2 and momentum continued into early July, then softened by about 200 basis points in the second half of July tied to the Cyclospora issue affecting the industry.
Adam Rymer said Q3 is the toughest lap this year and comps are expected around plus 1%.
Scott Boatwright said HEAP saves two to four hours of labor depending on volume and rollout targets 2,000 restaurants by year-end.
Scott Boatwright said company-owned openings are approximately 350 this year, about 80% with Chipotlane, and that he likes the 350 number.
financialHighlights: Revenue of $3.3 billion, up 9.3% year-over-year.
Digital sales of $1.3 billion, 38.3% of total sales, versus 35.5% in the prior year.
Restaurant level margin of 25.2%, down 220 basis points year-over-year.
Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.33, flat to last year.
Share repurchases of $631 million at an average $32.55 in Q2; year-to-date over $1.3 billion at an average $34.35.

keyMetrics.comparison: flat to last year; prior quarter $0.24

guidance: Adam Rymer, CFO, guides full-year comparable sales growth to low single-digit range, raised from prior guidance; prior prior-quarter guide was about flat.
Adam Rymer expects Q3 comparable sales around plus 1%, assuming the roughly 200 basis point Cyclospora impact continues; prior quarter Q2 guide was about +1%.
Adam Rymer expects Q3 pricing in the mid 2% range and full-year pricing near the high end of the 1%-2% range; Q3 inflation closer to about 3%.
Adam Rymer expects Q3 cost of sales just under 30% of sales, labor in the mid 25% range, and other operating costs in the mid 15% range.
Adam Rymer expects Q3 non-GAAP G&A around $180 million and FY2026 depreciation around 3% of sales with underlying effective tax rate 24%-26%.
Scott Boatwright expects approximately 350 company-owned openings in FY2026 and approximately 2,000 HEAP restaurants by year-end.
Scott Boatwright expects Seoul, South Korea first restaurants to open this year, Singapore to follow shortly thereafter in early 2027, and Mexico City expansion in 2027.

qa.question: What color can you give on the low single-digit 2026 comp guide, Q3 trajectory and the softening in recent weeks?
qa.answer: Traffic improved through Q2 and momentum continued into early July, then softened by about 200 basis points in the second half of July, tied to the Cyclospora issue. Q3 comps are expected around plus 1%, assuming the roughly 200 basis point impact continues, and Q3 is the toughest lap. Scott Boatwright, CEO, said Chipotle is not involved in the Cyclospora issue and its lettuces are sourced from California.

qa.question: Is the Q3 1% comp guide an underlying trend near 3% with a roughly 2-point Cyclospora headwind persisting through the quarter, and where is system Max 15 throughput?
qa.answer: The 1% guide assumes the roughly 200 basis point impact continues through the rest of the quarter, which Rymer said is very difficult to predict. HEAP restaurants do two or three more entrees in Max 15. summary.overview: Eli Lilly grew Q2 2026 revenue 48% year over year, with MOUNJARO and ZEPBOUND at $14.9 billion, up $6.3 billion, and non-GAAP performance margin at 54.8%. exchanges.question: How does Lilly see the consumer obesity market evolving and expanding treatment, and how similar is the US vs international self-pay market?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Obesity treatment utilization still mid-single-digit; access improving via Bridge and state Medicaid; ~3 million obesity TRxs; ~55% of ZEPBOUND prescriptions self-pay; expanding LillyDirect and consumer awareness. OUS obesity still mainly out of pocket; Lilly has launched versions of LillyDirect OUS, with models varying by local regulation.

exchanges.question: Why has the US Foundayo launch been slower than expected and when will it inflect; and OUS competitive dynamics vs Novo's oral, including UAE share given Novo's claimed 50% share in three weeks?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Focus on physician education, access and consumer awareness; CVS added Foundayo in June, Bridge launched July 1, full DTC started. Inflection seen last week of July, volume almost doubled vs a month ago, ~1 in 4 new starts on Foundayo. UAE launched early May, mostly incretin-naive patients; Lilly combined incretin share held steady despite second oral; Mexico and Saudi next, most launches in 2027, no supply gating; competitor data often sell-in with inventory build noise.

exchanges.question: What are requirements and milestones for retatrutide being accepted as a BLA, and would future incretins also qualify?
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes retatrutide is a biologic by amino acid count and analogous to a protein; first court decision was mixed, litigation active; hopes to reach conclusion with FDA. Clinical data complete but more CMC data needed; will update investors on filing status. Submission expected by Q1 next year. Did not address whether other incretins could qualify.

exchanges.question: Early learnings from Medicare obesity (Bridge) rollout, ramp curve, and orals vs injectables mix.
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Bridge expands access to ~35% more Americans; PA/approval process working well with CMS; LillyDirect enabled to fulfill Bridge. Inflection for ZEPBOUND and MOUNJARO over last few weeks; ~80% of Bridge patients on injectables; ~60%-70% are new patients without prior access.

exchanges.question: Is a commercial strategy needed against retatrutide currently available illegitimately, and does retatrutide's efficacy open new indications beyond tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: Expects patients to choose authentic retatrutide once approved. Knee osteoarthritis pain reduced ~75% (TRIUMPH-4, TRIUMPH-1); MASH/MASLD study ongoing leveraging glucagon mechanism; chronic lower back pain study reads out next year; evaluating further indications internally.

exchanges.question: Post-Verzenio breast cancer strategy; is an all-oral combo of SERD and oral PI3K planned?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Lilly believes it has best medicines for ER, CDK4/6 and PI3K alpha and plans to combine them. EMBER-4 adjuvant readout for INLURIYO next year; phase III for tersolisib about to begin, initially with existing endocrine therapy plus investigator's choice CDK4/6 (largely Verzenio), later combining with INLURIYO; all-oral combo envisioned.

exchanges.question: Guidance implies H2 revenue deceleration despite Bridge and Foundayo access; is it price or conservatism?
exchanges.answer: Guide raised by $2.5 billion (midpoint). Prior-period rebate/discount estimate adjustments, including this quarter, not expected to recur in H2. H2 2025 comp includes bolus of MOUNJARO country launches; future OUS growth from penetration; dollar growth still significant. Seasonality: Europe Q3 vacations, US Type 2 diabetes Q4.

exchanges.question: Which regions drive MOUNJARO OUS growth, and impact of generic semaglutide in India given capacity constraints?
exchanges.answer: China NRDL category leadership after 16 months; strong growth in Korea, UK, Mexico, Germany; share in many markets similar to or above US. MOUNJARO TRx still growing in India and Brazil after generic semaglutide; Canada tirzepatide TRx growing at market pace; generic makers face significant supply constraints.

exchanges.question: How extensive is Foundayo sampling and does it dampen IQVIA data; is the prescriber base expanding?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Samples cover first 30 days of first dose, extensive across prescriber base with full supply. Prescribers increased from 8,000 at last earnings to 36,000. Did not quantify IQVIA dampening effect.

exchanges.question: Obesity net price (~$580/script) above cash prices; how sustainable are medical exceptions with CVS back on formulary, and do they drive favorable rebate adjustments?
exchanges.answer: LillyDirect prices $299 to $449, Bridge at $245, plus commercial; script size also affects per-pack price. CVS access returns starting Q4; medical exceptions are short-term. Expects price to go down, embedded in guide, more than offset by volume growth.

exchanges.question: Are psychiatry and vaccines areas Lilly can scale and high priority, or one-off deals?
exchanges.responderTitle: President of Lilly Oncology and Head of Business Development
exchanges.answer: Common thread is immense unmet need, acquired at disciplined prices. Declined to forward-look on further building in infectious disease and psychiatry; will be opportunistic.

exchanges.question: Which one or two non-obesity pipeline assets deserve more attention?
exchanges.answer: Highlighted PCSK9 gene editing, oral and injectable Lp(a) drugs, psychiatry, vaccines, Centessa sleep-wake, addiction/MDD via incretins, Kelonia in vivo CAR T for multiple myeloma, AJ1-11095 JAK inhibitor, immunology growth and IBD/psoriatic combinations. Called it strongest pipeline ever.

exchanges.question: Foundayo UAE sales $31M vs $67M US suggest big ex-US obesity potential; and will ex-US governments reimburse it for diabetes better than tirzepatide?
exchanges.answer: Very early, noisy data with initial inventory build; majority of patients incretin-naive. Major OUS rollout early 2027. Slightly better positioned for Type 2 reimbursement with oral and three head-to-head trials, but OUS reimbursement takes time; launch focus is chronic weight management.

summary.overview: JPMorgan Chase reported Q2 2026 net income of $16.9 billion, EPS of $6.14 and ROTCE of 23%, with revenue ex significant items up 15% year-on-year and CIB revenue up 27% to $24.9 billion on an 86% rise in equities markets revenue. Jeremy Barnum, CFO, raised full-year NII ex-Markets guidance to about $96.5 billion from $95 billion and adjusted expense to about $107.5 billion, up $2.5 billion. Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, addressed the naming of co-presidents Doug and Troy and Marianne's retirement, saying his own timetable is unchanged.
keyTakeaways: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, said first-half capital markets outperformed prior expectations by $6.5 billion, with $1.5 billion of associated expense already booked and $1 billion implicitly added for the second half.

Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said conditions are 'getting close to as good as it gets' and Barnum called this quarter's equities combination (major IPOs, index rebalancing, Korean market dynamics, Asia activity) statistically improbable to repeat.
Dimon said two co-presidents were named to prepare them for more, Marianne chose to retire, and his timetable remains several years, plus or minus, up to the board.

Dimon said roughly $40 billion of excess capital is expected to be deployed over time at a 17% target return, called the earlier $20 billion M&A mention a mistake, and said the firm buys back less as the share price rises.

Dimon said JPM has almost 1,000 AI use cases with about 50 important ones, discrete areas have reduced jobs by 30-40% with most people offered other roles, and the ultimate beneficiary will be customers.
financialHighlights: Expenses were $27.3 billion, up 15% year-on-year, and credit costs were $2.5 billion including $2.4 billion of net charge-offs and a $149 million reserve build.
CIB net income was $9.7 billion with IB fees up 30%, fixed income markets up 6% and equities markets up 86% year-on-year.
CCB net income was $5.3 billion on revenue of $20.3 billion, up 8%, with average deposits up 3% year-on-year and over 500,000 net new checking accounts.
AWM net income was $2 billion at a 38% pre-tax margin, with revenue of $6.9 billion up 19%, $50 billion of long-term net inflows and AUM of $5.1 trillion, up 18%.
Standardized CET1 was 14.1%, down 20 bps quarter-on-quarter, with standardized RWA up approximately $103 billion.

keyMetrics.comparison: including significant items; $16.5 billion in Q1

guidance: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, guided full-year 2026 NII ex-Markets to about $96.5 billion (from $95 billion), total NII to approximately $105.5 billion and Markets NII to about $9 billion.
Barnum guided full-year adjusted expense to about $107.5 billion, raised $2.5 billion, driven mainly by volume- and revenue-related expense.
Barnum guided the full-year card net charge-off rate to approximately 3.2% and announced a $1.65 per share quarterly dividend effective Q3 2026.
Barnum kept consumer deposit growth at low single-digit for 2026, while Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, said a slowdown in expense growth might come in 2027 or 2028.
Dimon said smart cash tool tests will come out this year and that capital will be deployed at a 17% target return over time.

qa.question: Drivers of the NII ex-Markets revision, second-half cadence and exit rate, and why Markets NII rose despite higher rates.
qa.answer: NII ex-Markets moved from $95 billion to $96.5 billion, implying a higher exit run rate if forwards play out; the biggest driver is deposit balances plus mix shift toward higher margin, with consumer betas outperforming the model so actual sensitivity is probably above EAR. Markets NII is forecast up on fewer financed non-interest-bearing assets in the second half, and a higher CIB equity allocation moved roughly $150 million of NII from ex-Markets into Markets NII.

qa.question: Challenged the negative operating leverage framing and asked why Dimon says this is as good as it gets; also asked about Troy's fit for the consumer bank.
qa.answer: Dimon agreed dollar operating leverage was positive; Barnum said the $2.5 billion expense raise reflects $6.5 billion of first-half capital markets outperformance with $1.5 billion of expense booked and $1 billion implicitly added for the second half, and should not be over-read on revenue expectations. Dimon called the market very healthy and exuberant and said Troy was evaluated on analytics, EQ and culture carrying; Barnum corrected that Troy was an options trader, not FX.

qa.question: Whether AI could slow expense growth and improve operating leverage, and any developments on regulatory proposals.
qa.answer: Dimon called perpetual operating leverage a crazy notion, said expense growth might slow in 2027 or 2028, and listed four regulatory changes sought: removing double counts in operational and market risk capital ($80 billion-plus market risk capital vs a biggest-ever quarterly loss of $1.4 billion), adjusting G-SIB as intended since 2015, and fixing short-term wholesale funding treatment. Barnum said the SWF change disproportionately burdens JPM and Bank of America.
qa.read: Answered directly, pushed back on premise

qa.question: Consumer resilience and CapEx breadth, and why buy back at three times tangible book versus holding capital or pursuing M&A.
qa.answer: Consumer spend is fine across income segments with delinquencies a little lower than expected and little support for the K-shape narrative; Dimon cited AI CapEx rising from $400 billion to $700 billion this year toward a little over $1 trillion next year. Roughly $40 billion of excess capital is expected to be deployed over time; Dimon said the $20 billion M&A figure was a mistake and could be far more or nothing, with a 17% return goal.

qa.question: Whether competitors' credit underwriting is getting crazier, and whether regulatory stability could lift valuations.
qa.answer: Barnum said JPM passed on some data center deals over power supply and tenant risk; Dimon called deterioration mild — aggressive revenue assumptions, expense add-backs, more PIK, weaker covenants, rollover risk — and expects outliers in the next credit cycle. Barnum sees regulatory oscillations decreasing and is not convinced regulation is a major valuation drag.

qa.question: Whether this is as good as it gets, and whether there is a rate tipping point where deposit betas change.
qa.answer: Dimon said it is getting close to as good as it gets with unknown duration; Barnum said they do not know the tipping point, expected negative convexity in consumer rate paid earlier and it has not appeared, but common sense says it kicks in at some point.

whatChanged.toneShift: Jamie Dimon moved from Q1's 'nothing new or interesting' consumer framing to calling conditions 'close to as good as it gets' and the market exuberant, while Barnum shifted from 'the $105 is not a promise' to raising expense guidance outright. On capital, Dimon softened from buybacks being 'not our preferred way' to describing buybacks as an investment decision scaled to price.

risksMentioned: Jeremy Barnum, CFO, flagged yield-seeking deposit flows as a risk under a more hawkish rate environment and said the deposit beta tipping point is unknown.
Barnum said this quarter's equities combination is statistically improbable to repeat and the firm is a taker of an extremely risk-on market.
Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO, cited mild underwriting deterioration (more PIK, weaker covenants, rollover risk) and expects outliers in the next credit cycle.
Dimon flagged the negative real wage growth cohort as a watch area and said consumer credit depends on the labor market.
Barnum said the short-term wholesale funding treatment disproportionately burdens JPM and that the system is less flush with liquidity than capital.

exchanges.question: Asked Jamie to comment on management changes elevating Doug and Troy to co-presidents, leadership development, and implications for his CEO tenure. Follow-up to Jeremy on sustainability of investment banking and markets strength and how risk-on the businesses are.
exchanges.answer: Dimon: board decided to name two co-presidents to prepare them for more; timetable unchanged; Marianne chose to retire rather than stay when she learned of the plans; no mystery. Barnum: IB fees were fine but not at peak; some pull-forward and large ECM/IPO deals contributed meaningfully, but pipeline is quite robust and activity seems to beget more activity; won't guide. Markets revenues have been elevated for some time with much more financial resource deployment; the equities combination this quarter is hard to imagine repeating though the backdrop is supportive. The market is extremely risk-on and JPM is a taker of that, balancing client support with caution.

exchanges.question: Asked about CCB deposit growth, progress toward the 15% retail deposit share target and how higher-for-longer affects share gains. Follow-up on returns from branch, AI and banker investments, where the investment cycle stands, and medium-term operating leverage.
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposit growth strong in first half, outperforming expectations, helped by lending (BFI space, data centers) creating deposits. Consumer deposit expectation of low single-digit growth this year unchanged, balancing very strong net new checking accounts against yield-seeking flows, which remain a risk given the more hawkish rate environment. 15% share remains the aspiration as a long-term outcome of strategy (primary bank relationships, branch expansion, product deepening). Dimon: investment is a complete continuation of what they've done for years, expect no change; Barnum: franchise can invest aggressively while delivering exceptional current returns.

exchanges.question: Asked about drivers of the upward NII ex-Markets revision, Q3/Q4 cadence and exit rate into next year. Follow-up on why markets NII guidance rose despite higher rates.
exchanges.answer: NII ex-Markets revised from $95 billion to $96.5 billion for full year; implies higher exit run rate in the central case assuming forwards play out. Biggest driver is deposit balances across wholesale and consumer plus mix shift toward higher margin; rates slightly higher in short and long end, with actual sensitivity probably above EAR because consumer betas outperform the model. Markets NII is liability-sensitive but forecast up due to balance sheet composition, expecting fewer financed non-interest-bearing assets in second half. Equity allocation to CIB increased, moving roughly $150 million of NII from ex-Markets into markets NII, a rare case not offset in the bottom line.

exchanges.question: Asked what characteristics the board seeks in the next CEO and whether Marianne's departure extends Jamie's tenure — fixed vs rolling retirement date and longer executive chair stay. Follow-up asking what 'no change in timing' means.
exchanges.answer: Timing essentially the same and entirely up to the board. Listed qualities: management, people, analytical, detailed, culture carrier, curiosity, heart, grit, soul, work ethic, ability to travel and engage with operating centers, CEOs and prime ministers; wants leaders weighted across the whole company of 300,000 employees, 50,000 in branches, 150,000 in operating and call centers. Cited two exceptional co-presidents, Jen Piepszak as COO and Mary Erdoes running AWM. Timetable: whatever he said last time, several years, a few years plus or minus, up to the board.

exchanges.question: Asked whether, given AI and technology, expense growth could slow and operating leverage become more likely over the next few years, noting adjusted operating leverage was negative year-to-date. Follow-up on any developments on regulatory proposals, G-SIB surcharge and Basel III.
exchanges.answer: Dimon: margins went up this quarter; perpetual operating leverage is a crazy notion and partly why banks failed; might see a slowdown in expense growth in 2027 or 2028; AI benefits ultimately accrue to customers, not uniquely to JPM. Regulation: four changes — remove double count in operating risk capital, remove double count in market risk capital ($80 billion-plus market risk capital vs biggest quarterly loss ever $1.4 billion and CCAR market loss about $14-15 billion), adjust G-SIB as intended since 2015, and fix short-term wholesale funding treatment; happy to hold 10% more capital if asked but not via false numbers. Barnum: SWF change disproportionately burdens banks like JPM and Bank of America with both markets and consumer businesses versus former investment banks, damaging ability to serve Main Street.

exchanges.question: Asked whether this is as good as it gets or whether AI, defense spending and supply chain shifts make it earlier cycle. Follow-up on whether there is a tipping point in rates where deposit volumes and betas change meaningfully.
exchanges.answer: Dimon: getting close to as good as it gets; don't know how long it lasts. Barnum: don't really know the tipping point; expected negative convexity in consumer rate paid earlier in the cycle and it hasn't appeared, but common sense says it kicks in at some point. Stress tests model acceleration in rate paid under a regime change; empirical EAR is higher than reported, but ignoring convexity could falsely suggest a 7% rate environment is great. Dimon: they assume some of that in models.

exchanges.question: Challenged the negative operating leverage framing, noting dollar operating leverage was positive and marginal margins are high; asked why Jamie says this is as good as it gets. Second question on confidence that Troy, with a markets background, is right to run the consumer bank.
exchanges.answer: Dimon agreed dollar operating leverage was positive and rapid revenue increases drive big operating leverage. Barnum: expense guidance raised by $2.5 billion; first-half capital markets complex outperformed prior expectations by $6.5 billion with $1.5 billion of associated expense already booked; $1 billion implicitly added for second half, don't over-read it on revenue expectations. Dimon: market is very healthy, exuberant with high prices and volumes; could get better but unclear how much. On Troy: evaluated on analytics, EQ, culture carrying; showed expertise in markets, IB operations and technology; cross-company experience matters; Barnum corrected that Troy was an options trader, not FX.

exchanges.question: Asked whether banks vastly underestimate AI efficiency potential, citing Block cutting 40% of its workforce, and how JPM is positioning. Follow-up on what was most exceptional in equities this quarter and which areas may not be sustained.
exchanges.answer: Dimon: not a sensitive topic; expect huge efficiency in parts of the company; almost 1,000 use cases, about 50 really important ones across risk, fraud, marketing, hedging, prospecting, note-taking, idea generation, document reading; discrete areas reduced jobs by 30-40% with most people offered other jobs; retraining underway; July offsite will focus on it; benefits accrue to customers as competitors get AI via Fiserv, FIS and fintechs. Barnum: equities strength driven by widely reported factors — major IPOs, index rebalancing, complicated Korean equity market dynamics, Asia activity; statistically improbable that combination repeats though it could. Dimon: visible daily via NYSE, CME, hedge fund volumes and margin loans.

exchanges.question: Asked about Main Street consumer resilience, housing fragility and whether CapEx is broadening beyond AI. Follow-up on why buy back stock at three times tangible book rather than hold excess capital, and revisiting M&A appetite.
exchanges.answer: Some CapEx and loan growth appears non-AI but hard to untangle as AI proliferates; Dimon: CapEx about $4 trillion a year, AI went from $400 billion last year to $700 billion this year, projected a little over a trillion next year. Consumer spend fine across income segments with tax refund tailwind; delinquencies a little lower than expected across FICO bands; little support for the K-shape narrative; negative real wage growth cohort a watch area; consumer credit is about the labor market. On capital: buy back less as price rises; roughly $40 billion excess expected to be deployed over time given global infrastructure, remilitarization, trade restructuring, government deficits of 4.5-5%; buybacks are an investment decision. Dimon: $20 billion M&A mention was a mistake, could be far more or nothing; goal is deploying capital at 17% return; open to adjacencies and data-related deals; competition includes Goldman, Stripe, PayPal, Cash App, Block, Chime, SoFi, Revolut; hopes Chase UK becomes a great European digital bank.

exchanges.question: Asked for status and rollout timing of the smart cash tool and comments about paying more for money. Follow-up on European consumer banking aspirations in aggregate.
exchanges.answer: Smart cash tool is still a test case for a narrow segment of accounts where JPM competes for investment and deposit business; tests will come out this year. Europe: no bricks-and-mortar competition, but digital may have changed that; Chase UK started 4 or 5 years ago with almost 2.5-3 million customers; opened in Berlin and Germany is doing better than expected though not yet profitable; platform costs spread across countries toward breakeven. Added investment products in UK, likely elsewhere, plus probably credit card; dream is a pan-European digital bank leveraging private bank and cross-border clients.

exchanges.question: Asked what they see in competitors' credit underwriting and whether it is getting crazier. Follow-up on whether a period of regulatory stability could arrive and enhance bank valuations.
exchanges.answer: Barnum: data center underwriting is a bellwether; JPM passed on some deals on power supply and tenant risk using a precise framework; normal competitive pressures, some relationship lending to startup data center entities; JPM tries to hold the line. Dimon: deterioration is mild — aggressive revenue assumptions, expense add-backs, more PIK, weaker covenants, rollover risk — concentrated in some players; expects outliers in the next credit cycle. Regulation: Barnum sees oscillations decreasing toward stability with banks guided by their own risk appetite; not convinced regulation is a major valuation drag. Dimon: Supreme Court decision reduces flip-flopping; welcomes Bowman and Warsh review; focus on safety and soundness would leave no MRAs; resolution and recovery do not work, discount window should be rethought.

exchanges.question: Asked whether non-volume expense buckets like tech or marketing are also being raised or pulled forward. Follow-up on CIB capital allocation — peak allocation, internal limits, room to allocate more.
exchanges.answer: Some ups and downs including marketing strategy he won't disclose; main driver is volume and revenue related expense. Token expense is trivial in the first half and full year, with meaningful acceleration forecast in the second half; was budgeted and not a driver of the revision; strategy is right model for right purpose and open source where appropriate. Declined to discuss internal limits; capital allocation responds to client demand plus passive effects (volatility raising market risk capital, equity appreciation raising prime RWA); plenty of capital to serve clients where returns make sense. System is flush with capital but less so with liquidity; liquidity regulation adjustment needed to shrink Fed balance sheet. Dimon: risk standards haven't changed.
